hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 disruption of lipid metabolism, compared with APOE3, results in impaired late endosome/lysosome function.
A: APOE genotype or apoE isoform (APOE4 vs APOE3), acting through disrupted lipid metabolism (cholesterol, lipid droplets, sphingolipids)
B: late endosome / lysosome function (degradation, acidification, cholesterol egress, autophagic flux, lysosomal enzyme activity)
scope: IN: late endosome/lysosome function (cholesterol or lipid accumulation in lysosomes, NPC1, lysosomal degradation, cathepsin activity, lysosomal pH, autophagic flux, LAMP1 compartments) measured in APOE4 vs APOE3 cells, especially where linked to lipid/cholesterol metabolism; manipulations of lipid metabolism that change late-endosome/lysosome function in APOE4 cells. OUT: lipid changes with no late-endosome/lysosome readout, mitochondrial respiration alone, inflammation or transcriptomics alone.

proposed.reason_for_description: The contrast compares MβCD-treated APOE4 with vehicle APOE3 astrocytes, so genotype and a cholesterol-extraction drug change together and no clean change in A is isolated.

row.Finding quote: Consistent with improved lysosomal capacity, MβCD increased LysoTracker-positive lysosomal signal in APOE4/4 astrocytes (p = 0.044; Figure 5d), with similar effects observed across donors (2HβCD: p < 0.0001; MβCD: p < 0.0001, Figure S5d).
row.Finding summary: (MβCD-mediated cholesterol reduction in APOE4 astrocytes) -> (higher LysoTracker-positive lysosomal signal)

row.Finding description: Across three experiments with 7–10 images per line per experiment, APOE4 iAstrocytes showed greater cholesterol colocalization with dextran-labeled lysosomes than APOE3, with E4–E3 statistical significance unspecified.
row.Finding quote: Further colocalization of Filipin III with Dextran-Alexa 555 was highest in APOE4 iAstrocytes, indicating higher cholesterol levels in lysosomes of APOE4 iAstrocytes (E4 > E2) (Figure 3G).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (greater cholesterol localization in iAstrocyte lysosomes)
row.Experimental system: Human isogenic, monoallelic APOE3 (BIONi010-C-2) and APOE4 (BIONi010-C-4) iPSC-derived astrocytes after 44-day differentiation, at baseline. Cells received 0.2 mg/mL Dextran-Alexa 555 overnight followed by a 14-hour chase, 10 mM methyl-β-cyclodextrin for 30 minutes, fixation, and Filipin III staining for two hours. Confocal colocalization was normalized to APOE3.

proposed.why: Lysosomal cholesterol/lipid content is a surrogate B' for cholesterol egress (as in the organizers' exported-cholesterol example), and APOE4 could raise it through greater cholesterol delivery rather than impaired egress.

row.Finding description: Across three independent experiments, the lysosomal activity assay showed no significant difference between APOE4 and APOE3 iAstrocytes, although both had lower activity than APOE2 and APOE-KO cells.
row.Finding quote: Lysosomal activity in APOE3 and APOE4 was significantly lower than in APOE2 and APOE-KO cells (KO = E2 > E3 = E4) (Figure 4F).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in lysosomal activity in iAstrocytes)
row.Experimental system: Human isogenic, monoallelic APOE3 (BIONi010-C-2) and APOE4 (BIONi010-C-4) iPSC-derived astrocytes after 44-day differentiation, at baseline; lysosomal activity assay normalized to APOE3. The assay reagent, substrate, and assay duration are not specified in the supplied text.

row.Finding description: Across three independent experiments, LAMP2 immunofluorescence showed no significant difference in lysosome-covered cell area between APOE4 and APOE3 iAstrocytes.
row.Finding quote: Immunofluorescent detection of lysosomes by LAMP2 (Figure 4C) or Dextran-Alexa 555 (Figure S3) showed no difference between genotypes.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in LAMP2-positive lysosomal area in iAstrocytes)
row.Experimental system: Human isogenic, monoallelic APOE3 (BIONi010-C-2) and APOE4 (BIONi010-C-4) iPSC-derived astrocytes after 44-day differentiation, at baseline; LAMP2 immunocytochemistry with GFAP costaining, quantified as percentage of cell area. Compartment area provides a structural surrogate for lysosomal status.

row.Finding description: Western blots from three independent experiments showed significantly lower LAMP2 protein abundance in APOE4 than APOE3 iAstrocytes, providing a lysosomal-marker readout.
row.Finding quote: However, protein levels of LAMP2 detected by western blot were significantly higher in APOE3 compared with APOE2, APOE4, and APOE-KO (E3 > E2 = E4 = KO) (Figures 4D and 4E).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower LAMP2 protein abundance in iAstrocytes)
row.Experimental system: Human isogenic, monoallelic APOE3 (BIONi010-C-2) and APOE4 (BIONi010-C-4) iPSC-derived astrocytes after 44-day differentiation, at baseline; lysate western blots for LAMP2 and RAB5. This record concerns LAMP2; its quantification is presented in Fig 4E.

row.Finding description: Quantified LAMP1-positive lysosome staining per cell area was lower in APOE4 than APOE3 astrocytes (N=18 wells per genotype across two iPSC lines; p = 0.0311, unpaired t-test).
row.Finding quote: Compared to APOE3 astrocytes, APOE4 astrocytes showed decreased levels of all three downstream endosomal compartment markers (RAB11, RAB7, LAMP1) indicating dysfunction throughout the endocytic pathway.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (decreased LAMP1-positive lysosome staining in human astrocytes)
row.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived astrocytes from KOLF2.1J and AG09173 isogenic homozygous APOE3/APOE4 line pairs; four-day serum withdrawal before fixation and LAMP1 immunocytochemistry; representative confocal images.

row.Finding description: Increasing INPP5D expression in APOE4 astrocytes produced no significant difference in RAB7-positive late endosome staining compared with the darkGFP expression control.
row.Finding quote: Increasing either PICALM or INPP5D expression had no detectable effect on either RAB11-positive recycling endosomes (Figure 5E, 5F) or RAB7-positive late endosomes (Figure 5G, 5H).
row.Finding summary: (increased INPP5D expression in APOE4 astrocytes) -> (no change in RAB7-positive late endosome staining)
row.Experimental system: Human homozygous APOE4 iPSC-derived astrocytes from KOLF2.1J and AG09173; lentiviral INPP5D expression versus lentiviral darkGFP control, followed by serum withdrawal; fixed-cell RAB7 immunocytochemistry and confocal image quantification.

proposed.why: INPP5D overexpression within APOE4 astrocytes does not act on APOE, so no change in A is introduced; the readout is a structural compartment marker.
proposed.reason_for_description: INPP5D overexpression within APOE4 astrocytes does not act on APOE; RAB7 staining is a structural late-endosome marker.

row.Finding description: Increasing INPP5D expression in APOE4 astrocytes reduced LAMP1-positive lysosome staining compared with darkGFP control, without establishing whether lysosomal function improved or worsened.
row.Finding quote: Increased INPP5D expression did result in reduced LAMP1-positive lysosome staining compared to darkGFP (Figure 5I, 5J).
row.Finding summary: (increased INPP5D expression in APOE4 astrocytes) -> (decreased LAMP1-positive lysosome staining)
row.Experimental system: Human homozygous APOE4 iPSC-derived astrocytes from KOLF2.1J and AG09173; lentiviral INPP5D expression versus lentiviral darkGFP control, followed by serum withdrawal; fixed-cell LAMP1 immunocytochemistry and confocal image quantification.

proposed.why: INPP5D overexpression within APOE4 astrocytes does not act on APOE, so no change in A is introduced; the readout is a structural compartment marker.
proposed.reason_for_description: INPP5D overexpression within APOE4 astrocytes does not act on APOE; LAMP1 staining is a structural lysosome marker.

row.Finding description: Human isogenic iPSC-derived APOE4/4 oligodendroglia showed significantly more Bodipy-cholesterol colocalization with Lysotracker-Red than APOE3/3 oligodendroglia, with four biological replicates and four images averaged per replicate.
row.Finding quote: APOE4 oligodendroglia exhibited significantly (p = 0.0069) more Bodipy-cholesterol co-localized with Lysotracker-Red staining than APOE3/3, suggesting lysosomal accumulation of cholesterol in APOE4 oligodendroglia (Extended Data Fig. 7d).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (increased lysosomal cholesterol accumulation in human iPSC-derived oligodendroglia)
row.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived oligodendroglia from an isogenic APOE3/3–APOE4/4 experimental framework using reciprocal editing of a cognitively normal APOE3/3 donor line and an APOE4/4 AD donor line; the specific donor pair used for this panel is not identified in the supplied text. Cells were differentiated and matured in vitro; no aged-cell model was specified. Bodipy-cholesterol colocalization with Lysotracker-Red was quantified using ImageJ with identical thresholds across conditions.

proposed.why: Lysosomal cholesterol/lipid content is a surrogate B' for cholesterol egress (as in the organizers' exported-cholesterol example), and APOE4 could raise it through greater cholesterol delivery rather than impaired egress.

row.Finding description: Quantification in 12 mice per genotype assessed BODIPY-positive lipids within CD68-positive lysosomes, with the text reporting large microglial phagolysosomal accumulations in TE4 mice and no substantial glial lipid staining in TE3 mice.
row.Finding quote: Importantly, while we did not detect substantial levels of neutral or oxidized lipids in glia of TEKO or TE3 mice by immunostaining, large accumulations of BODIPY+ neutral lipids were observed within microglial phagolysosomes of TE4 mice.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4, with P301S tauopathy) -> (increased phagolysosomal neutral-lipid accumulation; impaired degradation inferred)
row.Experimental system: Hippocampal microglia in 9.5-month-old human APOE3- or APOE4-expressing PS19 P301S tau mice, murine Apoe-null background; C57BL/6-backcrossed P301S line; 6 male and 6 female mice per genotype; BODIPY/Iba1/CD68 staining and IMARIS compartmental colocalization analysis. No lysosomal degradation-rate, pH, or enzyme-activity assay was reported.
row.Data location: Fig. 2C; TE4-versus-TE3 contrast also explicitly described in the Discussion sentence beginning 'Importantly, while we did not detect substantial levels'

row.Finding description: At 8 months, APPPS1:E4 mice had higher frontal cortical LAMP1 immunoreactivity than APPPS1:E3 mice, interpreted as greater lysosomal accumulation, in groups containing 2–8 mice.
row.Finding quote: Additionally, APPPS1:E4 mice had higher levels of lysosomal accumulation at 8 and 16 months of age compared to APPPS1:E3 mice (Figure 7D).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher frontal cortical LAMP1-positive area at 8 months)
row.Experimental system: Eight-month-old C57BL/6-background mice heterozygous for APPswe/PS1dE9 and homozygous for human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted replacement; sexes pooled; frontal cortical sagittal sections; percentage area of LAMP1 immunoreactivity. LAMP1 accumulation was used to infer lysosomal dysfunction; lipid metabolism, acidification, and degradation were not tested.

row.Finding description: Replacing ApoE4-associated CE(20:4) with CE(18:1) significantly reduced neuronal acidic-compartment tau-fibril accumulation.
row.Finding quote: Indeed, CE(18:1)-lipApoE4 produced significantly lower accumulation of pHrodo-tau pffs than CE(20:4)-lipApoE4 (Figure 6L–M), consistent with lipofuscin-potentiated tau pff accumulation.
row.Finding summary: (ApoE4 cargo CE(20:4) -> CE(18:1)) -> (less endolysosomal tau-fibril accumulation)
row.Experimental system: Human NGN2 iPSC-derived neurons; 14-day 20 μg/mL lipidated ApoE4 pretreatment followed by 14 days of 2.5 μg/mL pHrodo-P301S-tau fibrils; ApoE replenished during incubation; confocal imaging.

proposed.why: Swapping the CE cargo within ApoE4 is a lipid manipulation, not a change in APOE isoform, and acidic-compartment pHrodo-tau signal mixes uptake with degradation.
proposed.reason_for_description: Swaps the cholesteryl-ester cargo of ApoE4 particles (CE(20:4) to CE(18:1)) within one isoform, a lipid manipulation that does not vary APOE genotype or isoform.

row.Finding description: Human neurons treated with PUFA-cholesteryl-ester–ApoE4 accumulated more lipofuscin than ApoE3-treated neurons after 21 days.
row.Finding quote: Therefore, we assessed the pathogenic potential of peroxidation-prone PUFA-CE by treating iNeurons with CE(20:4)-lipApoE isoforms. We observed accumulation of lipofuscin along with an established toxic product of arachidonic acid peroxidation, 4-HNE, following the allelic series of ApoE4 > ApoE3 > ApoE2.
row.Finding summary: (ApoE3 -> ApoE4 carrying CE(20:4)) -> (more neuronal lysosomal lipofuscin)
row.Experimental system: Human doxycycline-inducible NGN2 iPSC-derived neurons, Sigma 66540561; CE(20:4)/POPC-ApoE initially 20 μg/mL, replenished weekly with 10 μg/mL; 21-day exposure; autofluorescence imaging.

proposed.why: Lipofuscin is a lysosomal-storage surrogate that greater ApoE4 uptake of peroxidation-prone CE could raise without impaired lysosome function, so moderate like the other lipofuscin rows.

row.Finding description: Replacing peroxidation-prone CE(20:4) with CE(18:1) in ApoE4 particles abolished lipofuscin induction in human H4 cells.
row.Finding quote: Replacing CE(20:4) with CE(18:1) in the POPC-ApoE4 lipoproteins abolished lipofuscin induction (Figure 5J–K), denoting a PUFA requirement.
row.Finding summary: (ApoE4 cargo CE(20:4) -> CE(18:1)) -> (loss of lipofuscin induction)
row.Experimental system: Human H4 neuroglioma cells; three-day 20 μg/mL CE(20:4)/POPC-ApoE4 versus CE(18:1)/POPC-ApoE4 exposure; lipofuscin autofluorescence.

proposed.why: Swapping the CE cargo within ApoE4 is a lipid manipulation, not a change in APOE isoform.
proposed.reason_for_description: Swaps the cholesteryl-ester cargo of ApoE4 particles (CE(20:4) to CE(18:1)) within one isoform, a lipid manipulation that does not vary APOE genotype or isoform.

row.Finding description: After fourteen days, neuronal lipofuscin increasingly distinguished CE(20:4)-ApoE4 from ApoE3, with greater accumulation after ApoE4 treatment in three independent experiments.
row.Finding quote: After longer incubation (14 d and 21 d), a progressively larger difference between ApoE4 and ApoE3 emerged (Figure S5G, Figure 5B).
row.Finding summary: (ApoE3 -> ApoE4 carrying CE(20:4)) -> (more fourteen-day neuronal lipofuscin)
row.Experimental system: Human NGN2 iPSC-derived neurons; 14-day CE(20:4)/POPC-ApoE treatment, initially 20 μg/mL and replenished after seven days; autofluorescence imaging.
row.Data location: Supplementary Fig S5E and S5G, quantification

proposed.why: Same lipofuscin readout and isoform contrast as P4.F2, so same moderate strength.

row.Finding description: In three independent H4-cell experiments, CE(20:4)-ApoE3 and CE(20:4)-ApoE4 modestly but significantly reduced lysosomal cathepsin activity relative to low-lipofuscin treatments; an E4–E3 difference was not reported.
row.Finding quote: Cathepsin activity measured by the 6QC probe40 showed a modest but significant reduction with CE(20:4)-lipApoE3 or CE(20:4)-lipApoE4 treatment compared to other treatments that minimally induced lipofuscin (Figure S6G–H).
row.Finding summary: (CE(20:4)-ApoE4 versus low-lipofuscin treatments) -> (lower lysosomal cathepsin activity)
row.Experimental system: Human H4 neuroglioma cells; three-day CE(20:4)/POPC-ApoE isoform or CE(18:1)/POPC-ApoE treatment; 5 μM fluorogenic 6QC probe for two hours; live imaging of cathepsin-dependent fluorescence.

proposed.why: Cathepsin activity is lysosomal enzyme activity (B itself) and the treatments vary apoE isoform, so class 1 like the other direct lysosome-function rows.

row.Finding description: Replacing ApoE4-associated CE(20:4) with CE(18:1) prevented the neuronal lipofuscin phenotype in the tau-fibril accumulation experiment.
row.Finding quote: To confirm the effect of PUFA-CE-lipApoE4 on tau pff accumulation is causally linked to lipofuscin, we directly compared CE(20:4)-lipApoE4 with CE(18:1)-lipApoE4, which did not induce lipofuscin as CE(18:1) is not prone to peroxidation (Figure 6J–K).
row.Finding summary: (ApoE4 cargo CE(20:4) -> CE(18:1)) -> (less neuronal lipofuscin)
row.Experimental system: Human NGN2 iPSC-derived neurons; 14-day 20 μg/mL CE(20:4)/POPC-ApoE4 or CE(18:1)/POPC-ApoE4 pretreatment followed by 14 days with 2.5 μg/mL pHrodo-tau fibrils and continued ApoE replenishment; autofluorescence.

proposed.why: Swapping the CE cargo within ApoE4 is a lipid manipulation, not a change in APOE isoform.
proposed.reason_for_description: Swaps the cholesteryl-ester cargo of ApoE4 particles (CE(20:4) to CE(18:1)) within one isoform, a lipid manipulation that does not vary APOE genotype or isoform.

row.Finding description: Blocking receptor engagement with LDLR extracellular domain dramatically reduced ApoE4–PUFA-cholesteryl-ester–induced lipofuscin in human neurons.
row.Finding quote: LDLR ECD co-treatment with CE(20:4)-lipApoE4 dramatically reduced lipofuscin (Figure 5F–G), confirming LDLR dependency.
row.Finding summary: (CE(20:4)-ApoE4 + LDLR competition) -> (less neuronal lipofuscin)
row.Experimental system: Human NGN2 iPSC-derived neurons, Sigma 66540561; three-day treatment with 20 μg/mL CE(20:4)/POPC-ApoE4, with or without 20 μg/mL LDLR ECD; autofluorescence imaging.

proposed.why: LDLR extracellular-domain competition is a receptor manipulation within ApoE4 treatment, not a change in APOE isoform.
proposed.reason_for_description: Blocks ApoE4 particle binding with LDLR extracellular domain within one isoform, a receptor manipulation that does not vary APOE genotype or isoform.

row.Finding description: Human neurons pretreated with CE(20:4)-ApoE4 showed a trend toward more acidic-compartment tau-fibril signal than ApoE3-treated neurons (ApoE4 > ApoE3 > ApoE2 > K146E ApoE4), more pronounced among lipofuscin-positive neurons, across three independent experiments; the text calls it a trend and gives no P for the E4-E3 contrast.
row.Finding quote: After another 13–14 d incubation, total pHrodo signals from tau pffs that were internalized and accumulated in the endolysosomes demonstrated a trend of ApoE4 > ApoE3 > ApoE2 > K146E ApoE4, with the isoform-dependent difference being more pronounced among lipofuscin-positive neurons (Figure 6H–I), suggesting neuronal accumulation of tau pffs is augmented by a higher lipofuscin load.
row.Finding summary: (ApoE3 -> ApoE4 carrying CE(20:4)) -> (more endolysosomal tau-fibril accumulation)
row.Experimental system: Human NGN2 iPSC-derived neurons, Sigma 66540561; 14-day CE(20:4)/POPC-ApoE pretreatment, initially 20 μg/mL; 2.5 μg/mL pHrodo-labeled P301S tau fibrils for another 13 days; all neurons and cells with more than three lipofuscin spots analyzed.

proposed.why: Acidic-compartment pHrodo-cargo accumulation mixes uptake, acidification and persistence, so weak like the pHrodo-myelin persistence rows (P13.F6, P13.F11).

row.Finding description: CE(20:4)-ApoE3 and CE(20:4)-ApoE4 caused prominent LAMP1-positive lysosomal clustering in three independent H4-cell experiments; the text did not establish a difference between those isoforms.
row.Finding quote: LAMP1 immunostaining revealed no treatment effect on the total lysosomal area, but CE(20:4)-lipApoE3/E4 treatment resulted in prominent lysosomal clustering (Figure S6I–K), a phenotype previously observed in association with lysosomal impairment41,42.
row.Finding summary: (CE(20:4)-ApoE3 or ApoE4 treatment) -> (greater LAMP1-positive lysosomal clustering)
row.Experimental system: Human H4 neuroglioma cells after three-day lipidated ApoE treatment; fixed-cell LAMP1 immunostaining; clustering index calculated from clustered versus total LAMP1 spot area.

proposed.why: LAMP1 clustering is a lysosome-morphology surrogate like the other LAMP1/RAB7/CD68 marker rows, which are moderate.

row.Finding description: Introducing the Christchurch receptor-binding mutation into ApoE4 significantly attenuated PUFA-cholesteryl-ester–induced lipofuscin in human H4 cells.
row.Finding quote: Lastly, CE(20:4)-lipidated Christchurch mutants showed significantly attenuated lipofuscinosis (Figure 7F–G).
row.Finding summary: (ApoE4 -> ApoE4 R136S carrying CE(20:4)) -> (less lipofuscin)
row.Experimental system: Human H4 neuroglioma cells; three-day 20 μg/mL CE(20:4)/POPC-lipidated ApoE isoforms and Christchurch variants; lipofuscin autofluorescence imaging.

proposed.why: The Christchurch R136S mutation alters apoE4 receptor binding within one isoform; it neither varies APOE4 vs APOE3 nor is assumed to change it.
proposed.reason_for_description: Introduces the Christchurch R136S receptor-binding mutation into ApoE4, testing receptor binding within one isoform rather than varying APOE4 vs APOE3.

row.Finding description: In human astrocytes, ApoE4 produced greater internalized ApoE signals and occupancy of LAMP1 compartments than ApoE3; printed ApoE-positive LAMP1 fractions were 0.497 ± 0.090 versus 0.410 ± 0.049.
row.Finding quote: ApoE isoform differences were manifested in the differential levels of internalized lipApoE (ApoE4 > ApoE3 > ApoE2), giving rise to the same isoform trend for LAMP1-positive vesicles containing ApoE immunoreactivity (Mander’s coefficients = 0.266 ± 0.045 for ApoE2, 0.410 ± 0.049 for ApoE3, 0.497 ± 0.090 for ApoE4) (Figure 2I).
row.Finding summary: (ApoE3 -> ApoE4) -> (greater ApoE accumulation and ApoE occupancy of LAMP1 compartments)
row.Experimental system: Human APOE-KO iPSC-derived astrocytes originating from ThermoFisher A18945, originally APOE3/3; 10 μg/mL POPC-ApoE for one day; super-resolution immunofluorescence and Mander’s overlap analysis.

proposed.why: ApoE occupancy of LAMP1 compartments is a delivery/localization surrogate, scored moderate like P4.F15 and P22.F3-F5.

row.Finding description: Human H4 cells reproduced isoform-dependent lipofuscin accumulation after PUFA-cholesteryl-ester–ApoE treatment, with LDLR extracellular domain blocking the phenotype.
row.Finding quote: ApoE isoform-dependent lipofuscin accumulation was replicated in WT H4 and HAP1 cells, similarly blocked by LDLR ECD or KO of LDLR, but not LRP1 (Figure 5H–I, Figure S5H–I).
row.Finding summary: (ApoE3 -> ApoE4 carrying CE(20:4)) -> (greater lipofuscin burden)
row.Experimental system: Human H4 neuroglioma cells, ATCC HTB-148; three-day 20 μg/mL CE(20:4)/POPC-ApoE treatment, with or without 20 μg/mL LDLR ECD; autofluorescence imaging.

proposed.why: Same lipofuscin readout and isoform contrast as P4.F2, so same moderate strength.

row.Finding description: After seven days, ApoE3- and ApoE4-associated CE(20:4) produced weak neuronal lipofuscin whereas ApoE2 produced minimal signal, in three independent experiments; an E4–E3 difference was not stated.
row.Finding quote: At 7 d, lipofuscin induced by CE(20:4)-lipApoE3/E4 was weakly detectable, while signals for CE(20:4)-ApoE2 were minimal.
row.Finding summary: (CE(20:4)-ApoE3 or ApoE4 treatment) -> (early neuronal lipofuscin accumulation)
row.Experimental system: Human NGN2 iPSC-derived neurons, Sigma 66540561; seven-day 20 μg/mL CE(20:4)/POPC-ApoE exposure; live lipofuscin autofluorescence, normalized using endpoint nuclear counts.

row.Finding description: Lipidated ApoE treatments produced no reported treatment effect on total LAMP1-positive lysosomal area in three independent H4-cell experiments.
row.Finding quote: LAMP1 immunostaining revealed no treatment effect on the total lysosomal area, but CE(20:4)-lipApoE3/E4 treatment resulted in prominent lysosomal clustering (Figure S6I–K), a phenotype previously observed in association with lysosomal impairment41,42.
row.Finding summary: (Lipidated ApoE treatment, including ApoE3 and ApoE4) -> (no change in total lysosomal area)
row.Experimental system: Human H4 neuroglioma cells after three-day CE(20:4)/POPC-ApoE isoform or CE(18:1)/POPC-ApoE treatment; total LAMP1 spot area quantified by immunofluorescence.

row.Finding description: Internalized ApoE3 and ApoE4 localized predominantly to LAMP1 compartments, with printed Mander’s coefficients of 0.903 ± 0.024 and 0.900 ± 0.008, respectively; no significance comparison was reported.
row.Finding quote: Super-resolution imaging on APOE KO iAstrocytes confirmed internalized lipApoE completely colocalized with endogenous LDLR (Mander’s coefficient for ApoE puncta with colocalizing LDLR = 1 for all 3 isoforms), largely inside LAMP1 compartments (Figure 2H) (Mander’s coefficients for ApoE puncta with colocalizing LAMP1 = 0.823 ± 0.061 for ApoE2; 0.903 ± 0.024 for ApoE3; 0.900 ± 0.008 for ApoE4).
row.Finding summary: (ApoE3 -> ApoE4) -> (similar proportion of internalized ApoE localized to LAMP1 compartments)
row.Experimental system: Human APOE-KO A18945-derived iPSC astrocytes; one-day 10 μg/mL POPC-ApoE treatment; super-resolution ApoE, LDLR and LAMP1 imaging.

row.Finding description: ApoE3 and ApoE4 similarly promoted acidic-compartment HDL accumulation relative to ApoE2 or no ApoE, and LDLR extracellular domain suppressed both; an ApoE4-specific functional defect was not established.
row.Finding quote: Pre-complexing pHrodo-HDL with ApoE isoforms promoted its uptake in the order of ApoE4 ~ ApoE3 > ApoE2 (Figure 3A, C). LDLR ECD suppressed pHrodo-HDL uptake with ApoE3 or ApoE4, indicating a key role of LDLR in ApoE-mediated HDL internalization.
row.Finding summary: (ApoE3 -> ApoE4) -> (similar acidic-compartment HDL accumulation)
row.Experimental system: Human H4 neuroglioma cells; one-day treatment with 10 μg/mL pHrodo-HDL precomplexed with 10 μg/mL recombinant ApoE, with or without 20 μg/mL LDLR ECD; confocal imaging.

proposed.why: One-day pHrodo-HDL signal is mainly uptake, a weakly coupled surrogate scored like the other pHrodo-cargo accumulation rows.

row.Finding description: Following a three-hour myelin pulse, E4 microglia exhibited a significantly longer half-life of intracellular pHrodo-myelin fluorescence than E3 microglia, suggesting slower degradation of internalized myelin.
row.Finding quote: We also observe a significantly longer half-life of red fluorescence decay in E4 microglia relative to E3, WT and KO microglia, which were not significantly different from one another (Figure S4b, see Methods). This suggests that in addition to exhibiting increased phagocytic uptake, E4 microglia may exhibit impaired ability to degrade internalized myelin.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (longer internalized-myelin fluorescence half-life, suggesting impaired degradation)
row.Experimental system: Primary microglia from pooled P1–3 forebrains of homozygous human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice, C57BL/6 background; approximately four-week culture; three-hour pulse of 10 μg/ml pHrodo-red myelin followed by washout and hourly IncuCyte imaging for six days; phase-confluence-normalized fluorescence fitted with a one-phase exponential decay model using the six-hour fluorescence value as Y0; half-life calculated as ln(2)/K.
row.Data location: Supplementary Fig. S4B, E4 versus E3

row.Finding description: Following myelin challenge, E3 microglia significantly acidified their lysosomes whereas E4 microglia showed no significant further acidification and a nonsignificant pH increase, without a reported genotype-by-treatment interaction test.
row.Finding quote: Following treatment with myelin, E3 microglia significantly acidified their lysosomes (Figure S3). Interestingly, a similar decrease in lysosomal pH was observed in E4 microglia relative to E3 microglia at baseline. As lysosome function is optimal at lower pH, these effects may reflect activation of the lysosomal degradation machinery to cope with the increased burden of internalized debris following myelin challenge in E3 microglia, or in E4 vs E3 microglia even before myelin challenge. E4 microglia did not exhibit further acidification following myelin challenge but rather a slight (albeit not significant) increase of their lysosomal pH (Figure S3).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no significant further lysosomal acidification after myelin challenge)
row.Experimental system: Primary microglia from pooled P1–3 forebrains of homozygous human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice, C57BL/6 background; approximately four-week culture; untreated cells compared with cells exposed to myelin for three hours and assessed at 24 hours; lysosomal pH measured using LysoSensor and flow cytometry.
row.Data location: Supplementary Fig. S3; baseline-to-myelin pH responses, exact panels unavailable

row.Finding description: After myelin challenge, E4 and E3 microglia showed no significant difference in neutral-lipid colocalization with late-endosomal RAB7 across four independent experiments per group.
row.Finding quote: Low levels of colocalization between BODIPY and RAB7 were observed and no statistically significant difference across genotypes could be inferred (Fig. 3e), suggesting a portion of neutral lipids accumulated in early endosomes or other RAB5-positive organelles rather than RAB7-positive organelles.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in neutral-lipid colocalization with late-endosomal RAB7)
row.Experimental system: Primary microglia from pooled P1–3 forebrains of homozygous human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice, C57BL/6 background; approximately four-week culture; three-hour myelin challenge and analysis at 24 hours; BODIPY neutral-lipid staining and RAB7 immunofluorescence colocalization assessed using Pearson correlation, Fisher transformation, and a two-sample z-test.

row.Finding description: At baseline, E4 microglia had significantly more acidic lysosomes than E3 microglia, opposing a simple APOE4-associated failure of lysosomal acidification.
row.Finding quote: We then further used LysoSensor dye to measure the pH of lysosomes, which were significantly more acidic in E4 microglia when compared to E3 microglia (Figure S3).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower lysosomal pH at baseline)
row.Experimental system: Primary microglia from pooled P1–3 forebrains of homozygous human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice, C57BL/6 background; approximately four-week culture and enrichment; untreated baseline cells assessed using 2 μM LysoSensor Green DND-189 for 10 minutes and live-cell flow cytometry, with an intracellular pH calibration procedure described in Methods.
row.Data location: Supplementary Fig. S3; baseline E4-versus-E3 pH comparison, exact panel unavailable

proposed.why: Lysosomal pH measured with LysoSensor in APOE4 vs APOE3 cells is B itself, the same readout as P13.F2 and reference P18.F1 (class 1, strength 2).

row.Finding description: After myelin challenge, E4 microglia had greater LysoTracker fluorescence than E3 microglia across four independent experiments per group, interpreted as increased lysosomal mass.
row.Finding quote: E4 microglia again exhibited increased lysosomal mass relative to E3 microglia as measured by both Lyso-Tracker gMFI via flow cytometry (Fig. 3f) and CD68 immunostaining integrated density via fluorescence microscopy (Fig. 3g).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher LysoTracker-estimated lysosomal mass after myelin challenge)
row.Experimental system: Primary microglia from pooled P1–3 forebrains of homozygous human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice, C57BL/6 background; approximately four-week culture; three-hour myelin challenge followed by washout; LysoTracker Red DND-99 staining and live-cell flow cytometry at 24 hours.

row.Finding description: At 72 hours after myelin application, E4 microglia retained higher intracellular pHrodo-myelin fluorescence than E3 microglia across three to five independent experiments, consistent with greater cargo persistence but confounded by greater initial uptake.
row.Finding quote: Post-hoc t-tests at select time points identified significant differences (FDR adj. p-value = q < 0.05) between E4 microglia and microglia of other genotypes as early as 3 hours (E4 vs E3: q = 2.2 × 10−06, d = 3.7 CI95% [0.7, 6.6]; E4 vs KO: q = 1.1 × 10−06, d = 2.2 CI95% [0.3, 4.0], E4 vs WT, q = 2.6 × 10−06, d = 3.9 CI95% [1.1, 6.6]) and up to 72 hours (E4 vs E3: q = 0.001, d = 4.7 CI95% [1.7, 7.6], E4 vs KO, q = 0.1, d = 2.3 CI95% [0.4, 4.1], E4 vs WT, q = 0.03, d = 4.6 CI95% [1.4, 7.7]) post-treatment.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher persistent intracellular myelin fluorescence at 72 hours)
row.Experimental system: Primary microglia from pooled P1–3 forebrains of homozygous human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice, C57BL/6 background; approximately four-week culture and enrichment; three-hour pulse of 10 μg/ml pHrodo-red myelin followed by washout; normalized IncuCyte fluorescence measured 72 hours after initial application.
row.Data location: Fig. 2C, E4 versus E3 at 72 hours

row.Finding description: At 24 hours after myelin application, E4 microglia had higher late-endosomal RAB7 staining than E3 microglia across four independent experiments per group.
row.Finding quote: E4 microglia again displayed higher levels of both RAB5 and RAB7 relative to E3 microglia (Fig. 3c, d).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher late-endosomal RAB7 abundance after myelin challenge)
row.Experimental system: Primary microglia from pooled P1–3 forebrains of homozygous human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice, C57BL/6 background; approximately four-week culture and enrichment; three-hour myelin challenge followed by washout; RAB7 immunofluorescence integrated density per cell measured 24 hours after initial application.

row.Finding description: After myelin challenge, E4 microglia had higher CD68 staining than E3 microglia across four independent experiments per group, providing a surrogate for increased lysosomal mass.
row.Finding quote: E4 microglia again exhibited increased lysosomal mass relative to E3 microglia as measured by both Lyso-Tracker gMFI via flow cytometry (Fig. 3f) and CD68 immunostaining integrated density via fluorescence microscopy (Fig. 3g).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher lysosome-associated CD68 abundance after myelin challenge)
row.Experimental system: Primary microglia from pooled P1–3 forebrains of homozygous human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice, C57BL/6 background; approximately four-week culture; three-hour myelin challenge followed by washout; CD68 immunofluorescence integrated density per cell at 24 hours.

row.Finding description: At baseline, E4 microglia had higher RAB7 immunostaining than E3 microglia across four independent experiments per group, indicating greater late-endosomal marker abundance without establishing impaired function.
row.Finding quote: In addition, the levels of both early endosome (RAB5) and late endosome (RAB7) markers were increased in E4 microglia relative to E3 microglia (Fig. 1e), which may be reflective of an increased number and/or size of endosomes.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher late-endosomal RAB7 abundance)
row.Experimental system: Primary microglia isolated from pooled forebrains of P1–3 human APOE3 or APOE4 homozygous targeted-replacement mice, C57BL/6 background; enriched after approximately 28 days in mixed glial culture, replated and allowed to adhere overnight; baseline RAB7 immunofluorescence integrated density per cell. These are mouse cells expressing human APOE, not human brain cells.

row.Finding description: At baseline, E4 microglia had higher CD68 staining than E3 microglia across four independent experiments per group, providing another surrogate for increased lysosomal mass.
row.Finding quote: In addition, integrated density of fluorescent immunostaining of the lysosome-associated protein CD68 was increased in E4 microglia relative to E3 microglia, further demonstrating an increase in lysosomal mass (Fig. 1g).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher lysosome-associated CD68 abundance)
row.Experimental system: Primary microglia from pooled P1–3 forebrains of homozygous human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice, C57BL/6 background; approximately 28-day mixed glial culture followed by enrichment and overnight adhesion; untreated cells assessed by CD68 immunofluorescence integrated density per cell.

row.Finding description: Following a three-hour myelin pulse, E4 microglia showed higher intracellular pHrodo-myelin fluorescence than E3 microglia during six-day monitoring across three to five independent experiments, a composite readout of uptake, acidification, and cargo persistence.
row.Finding quote: E4 microglia exhibited significantly higher integrated intensity of red fluorescence relative to E3 microglia as well as microglia from mice homozygous for the WT or KO allele of mouse Apoe (Fig. 2b).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher intracellular acid-sensitive myelin fluorescence over time)
row.Experimental system: Primary microglia from pooled P1–3 forebrains of homozygous human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice, C57BL/6 background; enriched after approximately four weeks in culture; exposed to 10 μg/ml pHrodo-red-labeled wild-type mouse myelin for three hours, washed, and imaged hourly for six days using IncuCyte; fluorescence normalized to phase confluence.

row.Finding description: Across two experiments, Aβ1–42-induced lysosomal leakage occurred in more than 25% of apoE4-transfected cells versus 15% of apoE3-transfected cells.
row.Finding quote: Lysosomal leakage was seen in only 15% of the neo- and apoE3-transfected cells but in more than 25% of the apoE4-transfected cells (Fig. 2A).
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (greater proportion of cells with Aβ1–42-induced lysosomal leakage)
row.Experimental system: Mouse Neuro-2a neuroblastoma cells stably expressing human apoE3 or apoE4; Lucifer Yellow loading followed by aggregated Aβ1–42 at 20 μM for 20 h at 37 °C, as specified by reference to Fig 1; fluorescence microscopy scoring diffuse cytosolic staining across 15 fields, approximately 30 cells per field; two experiments.

row.Finding description: Aβ1–42 increased cytosolic β-hexosaminidase activity by approximately 85% in apoE4 cells and approximately 30% in apoE3 cells across two experiments performed in duplicate.
row.Finding quote: A treatment increased cytosolic -hexosaminidase activity to a significantly greater extent in apoE4-transfected cells than in neo- and apoE3-transfected cells (85% versus 40 and 30%, respec- tively; p  0.001).
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (greater Aβ1–42-induced release of lysosomal β-hexosaminidase into cytosol)
row.Experimental system: Mouse Neuro-2a neuroblastoma cells stably expressing human apoE3 or apoE4; grown to approximately 90% confluence and treated with aggregated Aβ1–42 at 20 μM for 24 h at 37 °C; cytosolic fractions isolated by homogenization and ultracentrifugation; β-hexosaminidase activity assayed in 20 μg cytosolic protein; two experiments in duplicate. This measures enzyme leakage, not loss of intrinsic catalytic activity.

row.Finding description: After aggregated Aβ1–42 treatment, more apoE4- than apoE3-transfected Neuro-2a cells showed diffuse Lucifer Yellow fluorescence, indicating greater lysosomal leakage.
row.Finding quote: After treatment with A1–42, however, it was readily apparent that more apoE4-transfected Neuro-2a cells than neo- or apoE3-transfected cells displayed a diffuse intracellular pattern of fluorescence, indicating lysosomal leak- age into the cytosol (Fig. 1, arrows).
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (greater Aβ1–42-induced lysosomal membrane leakage)
row.Experimental system: Mouse Neuro-2a neuroblastoma cells stably expressing human apoE3 or apoE4, generally secreting 80 ng apoE/ml medium/24 h; Lucifer Yellow loading at 100 μg/ml for 20 h, washing, then aggregated Aβ1–42 at 20 μM for 20 h at 37 °C; confocal microscopy. Aβ was aggregated for 72 h at 37 °C before use.

row.Finding description: In two experiments, apoE4 also increased Aβ1–40-induced lysosomal leakage relative to apoE3, although less markedly than with Aβ1–42.
row.Finding quote: ApoE4 also potentiated lysosomal leakage induced by A1–40 (Fig. 2A), albeit to a lesser extent than that induced by A1–42.
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (greater Aβ1–40-induced lysosomal leakage)
row.Experimental system: Mouse Neuro-2a neuroblastoma cells stably expressing human apoE3 or apoE4; Lucifer Yellow loading followed by aggregated Aβ1–40 at 20 μM for 20 h at 37 °C, following the Fig 1 protocol; diffuse cytosolic fluorescence scored in 15 fields, approximately 30 cells per field; two experiments.

row.Finding description: Without Aβ treatment, neither apoE3- nor apoE4-transfected Neuro-2a cells showed significant lysosomal leakage; no significant difference between isoforms was reported.
row.Finding quote: No significant ly- sosomal leakage was observed in untreated apoE3- or apoE4- transfected cells.
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (no change in detectable baseline lysosomal leakage)
row.Experimental system: Mouse Neuro-2a neuroblastoma cells stably transfected with human apoE3 or apoE4 genomic DNA, generally secreting 80 ng apoE/ml medium/24 h; untreated controls after Lucifer Yellow loading at 100 μg/ml for 20 h at 37 °C; confocal microscopy of punctate versus diffuse fluorescence. No donor age or human brain cells were studied.
row.Data location: Fig 1, untreated top row; Results, ApoE4 Potentiates Aβ-induced Lysosomal Leakage

row.Finding description: In mouse N2a cells, inhibitor-derived lysosomal Aβ42 degradation was greater with apoE3 than apoE4, with apoE3 producing 1.75-fold the degradation measured with apoE4.
row.Finding quote: When lysosomal degradation of Aβ42 was calculated by subtracting the cell-associated Aβ in the absence of inhibitors from that in the presence of inhibitors, apoE3 enhanced Aβ42 lysosomal degradation by 1.75-fold when compared with apoE4 ( Fig. 5 B ).
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (lower inhibitor-derived lysosomal Aβ42 degradation)
row.Experimental system: Mouse N2a neuroblastoma cells; recombinant human apoE3 or apoE4, 500 nM, with Aβ42, 500 nM, for 24 h in serum-free medium, with or without pepstatin A, leupeptin, and E-64d; degradation calculated as cell-associated Aβ42 with inhibitors minus that without inhibitors, using ELISA. Lipid metabolism was not measured.

row.Finding description: Inhibitor-derived lysosomal degradation of apoE4 was lower than that of apoE3 in mouse N2a cells exposed to Aβ42.
row.Finding quote: We found that apoE3 was transported into lysosomes and degraded more efficiently than apoE4 ( Fig. 7 , A and B ).
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (lower inhibitor-derived lysosomal apoE degradation)
row.Experimental system: Mouse N2a neuroblastoma cells; recombinant human apoE3 or apoE4, 500 nM, with Aβ42, 500 nM, for 24 h, with or without lysosomal inhibitors; degraded apoE calculated as cell-associated apoE with inhibitors minus that without inhibitors, using ELISA. Lipid metabolism was not measured.

row.Finding description: Confocal imaging of mouse N2a cells treated with lysosomal inhibitors showed less lysosome-associated Aβ42 with apoE4 than apoE3, with the image comparison quantified in Fig 5D.
row.Finding quote: In addition, confocal microscopy also revealed that internalized FAM-Aβ42, which was largely co-localized with LysoTracker, was greatly increased in the presence of apoE ( Fig. 5 C ). Upon quantification, we confirmed that the amounts of Aβ42 in lysosomes were higher in apoE3-treated cells than apoE4-treated cells ( Fig. 5 D ).
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (lower Aβ42 delivery to LysoTracker-positive compartments)
row.Experimental system: Mouse N2a neuroblastoma cells; FAM-Aβ42, 500 nM, and recombinant human apoE3 or apoE4, 500 nM, for 24 h with lysosomal inhibitors; LysoTracker Red, 75 nM, during the final hour; confocal fluorescence microscopy. This was a localization assay, not a calibrated lysosomal pH assay; lipid metabolism was not measured.
row.Data location: Fig 5C, representative images quantified in Fig 5D

row.Finding description: Quantification of confocal images showed less Aβ42 associated with lysosomes in apoE4-treated mouse N2a cells than in apoE3-treated cells during lysosomal inhibition.
row.Finding quote: Upon quantification, we confirmed that the amounts of Aβ42 in lysosomes were higher in apoE3-treated cells than apoE4-treated cells ( Fig. 5 D ).
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (lower lysosome-associated Aβ42)
row.Experimental system: Mouse N2a neuroblastoma cells; FAM-Aβ42, 500 nM, with recombinant human apoE3 or apoE4, 500 nM, for 24 h with lysosomal inhibitors; LysoTracker Red, 75 nM, during the final hour; ImageJ quantification of lysosome-associated Aβ fluorescence. Lipid metabolism was not measured.

row.Finding description: Immunostaining of mouse N2a cells during lysosomal inhibition showed less efficient trafficking of apoE4 than apoE3 to LAMP1-positive lysosomal compartments.
row.Finding quote: The more efficient trafficking of apoE3 than apoE4 was confirmed by immunostaining and confocal microscopy ( Fig. 7 , C and D ).
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (less efficient apoE trafficking to LAMP1-positive compartments)
row.Experimental system: Mouse N2a neuroblastoma cells; recombinant human apoE3 or apoE4, 500 nM, with Aβ42, 500 nM, for 24 h in the presence of lysosomal inhibitors; immunostaining for apoE and LAMP1 followed by confocal microscopy. Lipid metabolism was not measured.

row.Finding description: In the NH4Cl-confirmation experiments, Aβ-treated apoE4-expressing Neuro-2a cells had about fivefold greater cytosolic β-hexosaminidase activity than Aβ-treated apoE3-expressing cells.
row.Finding quote: In apoE4-transfected Neuro-2a cells, A1–42 increased cytosolic -hexosaminidase activity by about 5-fold com- pared with values in A-treated Neo- and apoE3-transfected cells.
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (greater Aβ-induced lysosomal enzyme leakage)
row.Experimental system: Human apoE3- or apoE4-transfected mouse Neuro-2a cells; Aβ1–42 challenge; cytosolic β-hexosaminidase activity in the text-only NH4Cl confirmation experiment.
row.Data location: Results, Low pH Required for ApoE4 Potentiation: sentence beginning 'In apoE4-transfected Neuro-2a cells'

row.Finding description: Raising lysosomal pH with NH4Cl reduced Aβ-induced lysosomal enzyme leakage in apoE4-expressing Neuro-2a cells to the range observed in Aβ-treated Neo controls.
row.Finding quote: NH4Cl treatment of the apoE4-transfected cells decreased lysosomal leakage induced by A1–42 to the range seen for A1–42-treated Neo- transfected cells.
row.Finding summary: (NH4Cl in apoE4 cells) -> (less Aβ-induced lysosomal enzyme leakage)
row.Experimental system: Human apoE4-transfected mouse Neuro-2a cells; 5 mM NH4Cl for 8 h to raise lysosomal pH; Aβ1–42 challenge; cytosolic β-hexosaminidase activity.
row.Data location: Results, Low pH Required for ApoE4 Potentiation: sentence beginning 'NH4Cl treatment of the apoE4-transfected cells'

proposed.why: NH4Cl is a drug acting on lysosomal pH within apoE4 cells and does not act on APOE, so it is not a surrogate A'.
proposed.reason_for_description: Treats apoE4 cells with NH4Cl to raise lysosomal pH, a drug that does not act on APOE genotype or isoform.

row.Finding description: LRP siRNA strongly reduced apoE4 potentiation of Abeta-induced lysosomal beta-hexosaminidase leakage in Neuro-2a cells (E4 cells: ~116% increase over control with Abeta vs ~48% with Abeta plus siRNA).
row.Finding quote: Notably, LRP siRNA very significantly reduced apoE4 potentiation of A-in- duced lysosomal leakage (Fig. 11B).
row.Finding summary: (LRP knockdown in apoE4 cells) -> (less Aβ-induced lysosomal enzyme leakage)
row.Experimental system: Human apoE4-expressing mouse Neuro-2a cells; LRP siRNA at 1.5 μg/ml with Lipofectamine; 20 μM Aβ1–42 added 48 h after transfection; assay at 72 h; cytosolic β-hexosaminidase.

proposed.why: LRP siRNA is a receptor knockdown within apoE4 cells and does not act on APOE, so it is not a surrogate A'.
proposed.reason_for_description: Knocks down the LRP receptor within apoE4 cells, a manipulation that does not act on APOE genotype or isoform.

row.Finding description: Aβ-treated apoE3- and apoE4-expressing cells showed similar fourfold increases in LAMP1 labeling, with no significant difference between isoforms reported.
row.Finding quote: ApoE3- and apoE4-transfected cells treated with A1–42 had a similar 4-fold increase in immunocytochemical labeling in the cells.
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (no change in reported Aβ-induced LAMP1-labeling response)
row.Experimental system: Human apoE3/apoE4-transfected mouse Neuro-2a cells; 20 μM Aβ for 0, 8, or 16 h; LAMP1 immunofluorescence images. The fourfold increases are within-group responses, not an E4/E3 ratio.
row.Data location: Fig 12C, quantification of the staining illustrated in Fig 12B; Discussion, page 9

row.Finding description: Isogenic human APOE4 astrocytes had lower SMPD1, NPC1 and NPC2 levels than APOE3 astrocytes, consistent with impaired lysosomal cholesterol export.
row.Finding quote: Negatively enriched Lysosome (Figures 2F and S3D) and lower SMPD1, NPC1 and NPC2 in APOE4 vs. APOE3 astrocytes (Figure S6D) indicates cholesterol transport out of lysosomes may be impaired by APOE4.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower astrocyte SMPD1, NPC1 and NPC2 levels)
row.Experimental system: Human hiPSC-derived isogenic APOE4 and APOE3 astrocytes in the cholesterol-trafficking experiments using Indiv1 and Indiv2, which share local haplotype hap.03. The available text identifies the measured regulators but does not specify this supplementary panel's assay, treatment duration or n.

row.Finding description: Sixteen hours after apoptotic-neuron injection, confocal imaging showed greater accumulation of LAMP1-positive lysosomes in APOE4-expressing than APOE3-expressing mouse microglia.
row.Finding quote: Immunostaining of microglia in the injection site showed accumulation of LAMP1+ lysosomes in IBA1+ APOE4-expressing microglia compared to in APOE3-expressing microglia (Fig. 1i,j).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (greater accumulation of LAMP1-positive lysosomes in microglia)
row.Experimental system: Mouse cortical and hippocampal microglia in 8-month-old human APOE3-knock-in versus APOE4-knock-in mice, without an APP/PS1 or P301S background in this experiment; fluorescent apoptotic primary mouse neurons injected stereotaxically, followed 16 hours later by confocal IBA1/LAMP1 immunostaining; lipid mediation and lysosomal degradation, acidification, and flux were not measured.

row.Finding description: APOE4/4 microglia produced significantly less fluorescence from a lysosomal degradation substrate than APOE3/3 cells, although reduced substrate uptake could contribute.
row.Finding quote: Since cathepsins play an essential role in lysosomal degradation, we further analyzed lysosomal activity in iMGs using flow cytometry with an Abcam’s proprietary self-quenched substrate and found that E4/E4 iMGs exhibited significantly lower lysosomal degradation activity compared to E3/E3 cells (Fig. 1G-H). Bafilomycin-treated cells served as a negative control (Fig. 1I). Lysosomal degradation activity can be influenced by the efficiency of substrate uptake into endosomes.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3/3 -> APOE4/4) -> (lower lysosomal substrate degradation signal)
row.Experimental system: Human APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia under basal conditions; Abcam ab234622 self-quenched substrate incubated for 1 hour; FITC-channel mean fluorescence measured by flow cytometry.
row.Data location: Fig. 1H; gating in Fig. 1G and APOE3/3 bafilomycin control in Fig. 1I

row.Finding description: After Aβ42 exposure, APOE4/4 microglia had significantly more galectin-1 puncta than APOE3/3 cells, indicating greater lysosomal membrane damage.
row.Finding quote: As shown in Fig. 4F, H, the formation of galectin puncta, detected with galectin (LGALS)-1-specific antibody, was significantly higher in E4/E4 iMGs than in E3/E3 iMGs after Aβ42 exposure, indicating increased lysosomal leakage in E4/E4 iMGs.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3/3 -> APOE4/4 under Aβ42) -> (greater lysosomal membrane permeabilization)
row.Experimental system: Human APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia; 200 nM soluble Aβ42 oligomer preparation for 48 hours; LGALS1 immunostaining and confocal galectin-puncta assay. Puncta were normalized to nuclei; the Methods reports three images per line per treatment, not the number of lines.

proposed.why: Galectin puncta measure lysosomal membrane damage, not one of B's listed functions, so it is a surrogate B'; damaged lysosomes are dysfunctional, so the surrogate is tightly coupled (strength 2).

row.Finding description: Bafilomycin-based LC3-II:LC3-I measurements showed no significant difference in basal autophagic flux between APOE4/4 and APOE3/3 microglia.
row.Finding quote: As expected, blocking autophagic flux by inhibiting lysosomal acidification with bafilomycin A led to increased LC3-II: LC3-I ratio compared to the basal levels (Fig. 1C, D), but there was no significant difference between the genotypes.
row.Finding summary: No significant genotype difference was detected in basal autophagic flux.
row.Experimental system: Human APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia; basal cultures compared with bafilomycin A1 treatment for 3 hours; immunoblot LC3-II:LC3-I ratios used to assess autophagic flux.

row.Finding description: Rapamycin-induced autophagic-flux measurements showed no significant difference between APOE4/4 and APOE3/3 microglia.
row.Finding quote: Similarly, treatment with rapamycin, an inhibitor of the mTORC1 complex and a well-known autophagy inducer, did not reveal any significant differences between the genotypes (Fig. 1C, E).
row.Finding summary: No significant genotype difference was detected in rapamycin-induced autophagic flux.
row.Experimental system: Human APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia; 100 nM rapamycin for 6 hours, with or without bafilomycin A1; LC3 immunoblotting and LC3-II:LC3-I ratios.

row.Finding description: LAMP2 protein tended to be lower in APOE4/4 than APOE3/3 microglia, but the text does not establish a significant genotype difference.
row.Finding quote: Interestingly, lysosomal-associated membrane protein 2 (LAMP-2), a key mediator of autophagosome-lysosome fusion [57, 58], was unaffected by Aβ42 stimulation but tended to be reduced in E4/E4 iMGs (Fig. 4D, E).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3/3 -> APOE4/4) -> (trend toward lower LAMP2 protein)
row.Experimental system: Human APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia; basal and 48-hour 200 nM soluble Aβ42 conditions, with bafilomycin conditions also shown; LAMP2 immunoblotting. LAMP2 abundance is a surrogate for lysosomal content/fusion capacity, not a direct fusion measurement.
row.Data location: Fig. 4D (LAMP2, NT bars), 4E; supplementary raw-blot PDF page 11

row.Finding description: Basal proteomics comparing two mutually isogenic APOE4/4 lines with APOE3/3 lines found lower MFSD1 protein, a lysosomal-content surrogate.
row.Finding quote: Since proteomic analysis comparing two (isogenic to each other) E4/E4 lines to E3/E3 lines revealed a downregulation of two other lysosomal proteins MFSD1 and GLMP in E4/E4 iMGs at basal conditions (Fig. 3B, Table S4), the overall lysosomal protein content may be reduced by E4/E4 genotype.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3/3 -> APOE4/4) -> (lower basal lysosomal MFSD1 protein)
row.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived microglia under basal conditions; DIA-PASEF LC-MS/MS proteomics. Two APOE4/4 lines were isogenic to each other; this does not establish that the entire APOE4/4-versus-APOE3/3 comparison was isogenic. Sample size 2 counts the reported APOE4/4 lines only.

row.Finding description: Aβ42-associated LC3-II accumulation showed no significant difference between APOE4/4 and APOE3/3 microglia.
row.Finding quote: Further, we analyzed LC3-II levels by WB, and found that, similarly to LPS/IFNγ stimulation, Aβ42 strongly increased intracellular LC3-II (p = 0.04), irrespective of the APOE genotype (Fig. 4B, C).
row.Finding summary: Aβ42 increased LC3-II, with no significant genotype difference reported.
row.Experimental system: Human APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia; 200 nM soluble Aβ42 oligomer preparation for 48 hours; LC3-II immunoblotting. The preparation contained measurable endotoxin.

row.Finding description: Under basal conditions, human APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia had significantly lower LC3-II protein levels than APOE3/3 cells, a surrogate that does not itself establish impaired lysosomal degradation.
row.Finding quote: Under basal conditions, E4/E4 iMGs exhibited significantly lower LC3-II levels compared to E3/E3 cells (Fig. 1A, B).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3/3 -> APOE4/4) -> (lower basal LC3-II in human iPSC-derived microglia)
row.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived microglia from multiple APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 lines, including an isogenic pair; unstimulated cultures; LC3 immunoblotting. The study-wide eight APOE3/3 and six APOE4/4 lines are not a panel-specific sample size. Available donor ages include 63–80 years; cellular aging was not experimentally established.
row.Data location: Fig. 1A,B; corresponding uncropped LC3 blots in supplementary PDF pages 1–3, 6, 8–9

row.Finding description: After 48 hours of LPS/IFNγ stimulation, LC3-II accumulation showed no significant difference between APOE4/4 and APOE3/3 microglia.
row.Finding quote: Consistent with the proteomics data, this WB analysis confirmed that 48-h stimulation with LPS/IFNγ strongly increased the accumulation of LC3-II as well as glutamine synthetase (GLUL), although the protein levels were not affected by the APOE genotype (Fig. 3C, D).
row.Finding summary: No significant genotype difference was reported in LC3-II accumulation after LPS/IFNγ.
row.Experimental system: Human APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia; 50 ng/ml LPS plus 15 ng/ml IFNγ for 48 hours; LC3-II immunoblotting in an experiment independent of the proteomics.

row.Finding description: Blocking endosome maturation and degradation with apilimod increased dextran accumulation in both APOE4/4 and APOE3/3 microglia; the legend reports N=3 iPSC lines.
row.Finding quote: Moreover, when endosome maturation and degradation were blocked by apilimod, a significant accumulation of dextran was observed over 24 h, irrespective of the APOE genotype (repeated measures ANOVA, time x treatment p < 0.001, Fig. 1M).
row.Finding summary: Apilimod increased dextran accumulation irrespective of APOE genotype. P < 0.001 applies to time × treatment.
row.Experimental system: Human APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia; 0.683 µM apilimod versus DMSO vehicle; pHrodo-dextran fluorescence accumulation reported over 24 hours. The legend's N=3 iPSC lines does not specify allocation by genotype.

proposed.reason_for_description: The manipulation is apilimod (a PIKfyve inhibitor) applied within each genotype and does not act on APOE, so no class 1-4 form fits; the genotype comparison showed no interaction.

row.Finding description: Basal pHrodo-dextran fluorescence accumulated less in APOE4/4 than APOE3/3 microglia over time, but this assay cannot separate reduced uptake from altered acidification.
row.Finding quote: To assess pinocytosis (fluid-phase endocytosis), we added pHrodo-conjugated dextran (MW 10 kDa) and monitored intracellular fluorescence over 20 h using the IncuCyte live imaging system (Fig. 1J, K). Under basal conditions, pinocytosis was significantly reduced in E4/E4 iMGs compared to E3/E3 iMGs (two-way repeated measures ANOVA, time x genotype p = 0.01; Fig. 1J, L).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3/3 -> APOE4/4) -> (lower basal pHrodo-dextran signal in endolysosomal compartments)
row.Experimental system: Human APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia; basal exposure to 10 kDa pHrodo-dextran at 16.7–20 µg/ml; IncuCyte fluorescence monitoring over 20 hours, normalized to cell confluence. This is an uptake/acidic-compartment surrogate, not a calibrated lysosomal-pH assay.
row.Data location: Fig. 1J,K; Results associates the longitudinal test with Fig. 1J,L, whereas the legend assigns the time-course quantification to K

row.Finding description: Under basal conditions, TOM-20 protein showed no significant difference between APOE4/4 and APOE3/3 microglia, providing an indirect mitochondrial-mass/mitophagy readout.
row.Finding quote: Under basal conditions or after treatment with bafilomycin A, there were no differences in TOM-20 protein levels between the genotypes (Supplementary Fig. 2C).
row.Finding summary: No significant genotype difference was reported in basal TOM-20.
row.Experimental system: Human APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia; basal cultures; TOM-20 immunoblotting as a mitochondrial-mass surrogate used by the authors to assess mitophagy.
row.Data location: Supplementary Fig. 2C; supplementary raw-blot PDF pages 2–3

row.Finding description: After rapamycin treatment, mitochondrial mass assessed through TOM-20 showed no significant difference between APOE4/4 and APOE3/3 microglia.
row.Finding quote: Similarly, treatment with rapamycin, with or without bafilomycin A, did not reveal any differences in mitochondrial mass between the genotypes, suggesting similar levels of mitophagy (Supplementary Fig. 2D).
row.Finding summary: No significant genotype difference was reported in TOM-20-assessed mitochondrial mass after rapamycin.
row.Experimental system: Human APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia; 100 nM rapamycin for 6 hours; TOM-20 immunoblotting as an indirect mitochondrial-mass/mitophagy readout.
row.Data location: Supplementary Fig. 2D; supplementary raw-blot PDF pages 4–5, 7

row.Finding description: Uptake of pHrodo-conjugated zymosan-coated beads showed no significant difference between APOE4/4 and APOE3/3 microglia, although this acid-dependent uptake signal is only an indirect lysosomal surrogate.
row.Finding quote: Interestingly, the APOE genotype did not significantly affect the uptake of pHrodo-conjugated zymosan-coated beads (Supplementary Fig. 2E-G) or fibrillar Aβ42 (Supplementary Fig. 2H, I).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3/3 -> APOE4/4) -> (no change in pHrodo-zymosan uptake signal)
row.Experimental system: Human APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia; pHrodo-conjugated zymosan-coated bead uptake assay. The supplied text does not specify panel-by-panel content, incubation duration or biological sample size. Uptake and phagolysosomal acidification are unresolved.

row.Finding description: Young APOE4 mice had significantly more hippocampal neuronal lysosomal compartments than APOE3 mice in five mice per sex/genotype group.
row.Finding quote: Furthermore, while both neuronal EE’s and LE’s showed an increasing pattern with APOE genotype, only N-LY’s showed a significant upregulation in APOE4 (APOE2<E4;E3<E4).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4, young hippocampus) -> (higher neuronal LAMP1-compartment abundance)
row.Experimental system: Male and female human-APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 mice, 5–6 months; fixed CA1 hippocampus; LAMP1 objects within NeuN soma per neuronal volume; no direct degradation, pH, enzyme-activity, or flux assay.

row.Finding description: Young cortical neuronal lysosomal cholesterol showed no significant APOE-dependent change in five mice per sex/genotype group.
row.Finding quote: At the same time, N-LE-Ch levels showed similar expression to N-LE’s, while N-LY-Ch levels did not show an APOE dependent change.
row.Finding summary: (APOE genotype variation including APOE3 -> APOE4, young cortex) -> (no change in neuronal lysosomal cholesterol colocalization reaching significance)
row.Experimental system: Male and female human-APOE2/2, APOE3/3, and APOE4/4 mice, 5–6 months; fixed neocortex; neuronal D4H* spots overlapping LAMP1, normalized to neuronal D4H* spots and NeuN volume.

row.Finding description: Young hippocampal neuronal late-endosomal cholesterol and total and neuronal lysosomal cholesterol showed no significant APOE-genotype differences in five mice per sex/genotype group.
row.Finding quote: There was also a decrease in T-LE-Ch in APOE3<E2, with no change in APOE4, and N-LE-Ch levels were not affected. Similar to the cortex, there was no effect of APOE genotype on total or neuronal LY-Ch, even though neuronal LY levels were increased, indicating that this upregulation is not linked to the LY capacity to process cholesterol.
row.Finding summary: (APOE genotype variation including APOE3 -> APOE4, young hippocampus) -> (no change in neuronal late-endosomal or total/neuronal lysosomal cholesterol reaching significance)
row.Experimental system: Male and female human-APOE knock-in mice, 5–6 months; fixed CA1 hippocampus; D4H*–CD63 or D4H*–LAMP1 colocalization fractions normalized to DAPI nuclei or NeuN volume; no direct processing-capacity assay.
row.Data location: Fig 4E, neuronal late-endosomal and total/neuronal lysosomal cholesterol

row.Finding description: Young entorhinal total and neuronal lysosomal cholesterol showed no significant APOE-genotype difference in five mice per sex/genotype group.
row.Finding quote: There was a striking decrease in both total and neuronal EE-Ch and LE-Ch (APOE4<E2), while there was a complete absence of APOE effect on LY-Ch levels (Fig. 4F).
row.Finding summary: (APOE genotype variation including APOE3 -> APOE4, young entorhinal cortex) -> (no change in lysosomal cholesterol colocalization reaching significance)
row.Experimental system: Male and female human-APOE2/2, APOE3/3, and APOE4/4 mice, 5–6 months; fixed entorhinal cortex; total and neuronal D4H*–LAMP1 colocalization fractions normalized to nuclei or neuronal volume.
row.Data location: Fig 4F, total and neuronal lysosomal cholesterol

row.Finding description: Young female APOE4 mice had significantly higher hippocampal total late-endosomal cholesterol colocalization than young female APOE3 mice in five mice per sex/genotype group.
row.Finding quote: Total LE-Ch was decreased in APOE3 females compared to APOE2 and APOE4, as well as APOE3 males.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4, young females) -> (higher hippocampal total late-endosomal cholesterol colocalization)
row.Experimental system: Female human-APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 mice, 5–6 months; fixed CA1 hippocampus; total D4H* spots colocalized with CD63 divided by total D4H* spots and DAPI nuclei; cholesterol accumulation/egress inferred from static localization.
row.Data location: Fig 9D, total late-endosomal cholesterol, young females

row.Finding description: Young (5-6 months) female APOE4 mice had significantly higher cortical neuronal lysosomal cholesterol than young female APOE3 mice (also higher than APOE2 females and APOE4 males), five mice per sex/genotype/age group.
row.Finding quote: The only significant difference measured on N-LY-Ch levels was in the APOE4 females, which showed a significant increase compared to APOE2 and APOE3 females, and APOE4 males in the cortex (Fig. 10B).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4, young females) -> (higher cortical neuronal lysosomal cholesterol colocalization)
row.Experimental system: Female human-APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 knock-in mice, 5-6 months (young panel of Fig 10B); fixed neocortex; neuronal D4H*-LAMP1 colocalization fraction divided by NeuN volume.
row.Data location: Fig 10B, Young panel, neuronal lysosomal cholesterol

row.Finding description: Young hippocampal total late-endosome and lysosome abundance showed no significant APOE-genotype effect, and neuronal late-endosome increases were not significant, in five mice per sex/genotype group.
row.Finding quote: In the HIPP, the total levels of EE’s, LE’s, and LY’s were not affected by APOE genotype (Fig. 4B). Furthermore, while both neuronal EE’s and LE’s showed an increasing pattern with APOE genotype, only N-LY’s showed a significant upregulation in APOE4 (APOE2<E4;E3<E4).
row.Finding summary: (APOE genotype variation including APOE3 -> APOE4, young hippocampus) -> (no change in total late-endosome/lysosome or neuronal late-endosome abundance reaching significance)
row.Experimental system: Male and female human-APOE2/2, APOE3/3, and APOE4/4 mice, 5–6 months; fixed CA1 hippocampus; total CD63/LAMP1 objects per DAPI nucleus and neuronal CD63 spots per NeuN volume.
row.Data location: Fig 4B, total CD63/LAMP1 and neuronal CD63 measurements

row.Finding description: Young entorhinal total and neuronal lysosome abundance showed no significant APOE-genotype difference in five mice per sex/genotype group.
row.Finding quote: Both total and neuronal LE’s were decreased in APOE4<E2, while lysosomes were not affected by APOE genotype.
row.Finding summary: (APOE genotype variation including APOE3 -> APOE4, young entorhinal cortex) -> (no change in lysosome abundance reaching significance)
row.Experimental system: Male and female human-APOE2/2, APOE3/3, and APOE4/4 mice, 5–6 months; fixed entorhinal cortex; total LAMP1 objects per DAPI nucleus and neuronal LAMP1 objects per NeuN volume.
row.Data location: Fig 4C, total and neuronal LAMP1 measurements

row.Finding description: Young entorhinal total and neuronal late-endosomal cholesterol were qualitatively lower in APOE4 than intermediate APOE3 levels in five mice per sex/genotype group, while the stated significant contrast was APOE4 versus APOE2.
row.Finding quote: The largest effect was observed in the young EC, with neuronal LE’s, EE’s, as well as total/neuronal EE-Ch and LE-Ch decreasing in APOE4<APOE2 (while APOE3 levels were in between).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4, young entorhinal cortex) -> (qualitatively lower total and neuronal late-endosomal cholesterol colocalization)
row.Experimental system: Male and female human-APOE knock-in mice, 5–6 months; fixed entorhinal cortex; total and neuronal D4H*–CD63 colocalization fractions divided by DAPI nuclei or NeuN volume.
row.Data location: Fig 4F; Discussion, APOE genotype effects at young age

proposed.why: Same D4H*-CD63 late-endosomal cholesterol colocalization readout and APOE3-vs-APOE4 comparison as P34.F5 (3/3); strength reflects the surrogate, not the statistical support.

row.Finding description: Female APOE4 mice had significantly greater entorhinal neuronal lysosome abundance than female APOE3 mice in five mice per sex/genotype/age group, with ages pooled.
row.Finding quote: However, paired contrasts showed that N-LY’s in the EC were increased in APOE4 female compared to male mice, and compared to APOE3 females.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4, females) -> (higher entorhinal neuronal LAMP1-compartment abundance)
row.Experimental system: Female human-APOE3/3 and APOE4/4 mice from young, middle-aged, and old groups; age-adjusted pooled analysis; fixed entorhinal cortex; neuronal LAMP1 objects per NeuN volume.
row.Data location: Fig 7C, entorhinal neuronal lysosomes, female APOE4 versus APOE3

row.Finding description: Entorhinal total and neuronal late-endosome abundance showed no significant three-way interaction or pairwise differences across sex, age, and APOE genotype in five mice per sex/genotype/age group.
row.Finding quote: In the EC, there were no significant three-way interactions observed affecting CD63 LE levels, and no pairwise differences were detected (Fig. 9E).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4, sex- and age-stratified entorhinal cortex) -> (no change in late-endosome abundance reaching significance)
row.Experimental system: Male and female human-APOE2/2, APOE3/3, and APOE4/4 mice, three ages; fixed entorhinal cortex; total CD63 spots per DAPI nucleus and neuronal CD63 spots per NeuN volume.

row.Finding description: Entorhinal total lysosomal cholesterol showed no significant differences in the sex-, age-, and APOE-stratified analysis of five mice per sex/genotype/age group.
row.Finding quote: There were no differences in total LY-Ch levels in the EC (Fig. 10F).
row.Finding summary: (APOE genotype variation including APOE3 -> APOE4, entorhinal cortex) -> (no change in total lysosomal cholesterol colocalization reaching significance)
row.Experimental system: Male and female human-APOE2/2, APOE3/3, and APOE4/4 mice, three ages; fixed entorhinal cortex; total D4H* spots overlapping LAMP1 divided by total D4H* spots and DAPI nuclei.

row.Finding description: After rapamycin, APOE4 microglia displayed less tandem-LC3 reporter conversion to red-only puncta than APOE3 microglia, interpreted as impaired autophagosome delivery to lysosomes.
row.Finding quote: Thus, autophagosomes delivery to lysosomes is hampered in APOE4 microglia.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (less autophagosome delivery to lysosomes)
row.Experimental system: Murine N9 microglia stably expressing human FLAG-APOE3 or FLAG-APOE4 and transiently transfected with tandem LC3-EGFP-mRFP; 48 h after transfection, 150 nM rapamycin for 24 h; confocal microscopy of yellow and red-only puncta. No lipid-metabolism assay.

proposed.why: Same tandem LC3 reporter (red-only vs yellow puncta) readout as the other APOE3-vs-APOE4 tandem-LC3 rows: autophagic flux/autolysosome formation is B itself and A is the APOE isoform, so class 1 strength 2 like the checked lysosomal-pH reference row.

row.Finding description: Following rapamycin, the reported red-only LC3 fraction was lower in APOE4 than APOE3 microglia, 13.84% ± 1.96 versus 41.03% ± 3.268, with at least 50 cells per treatment analyzed.
row.Finding quote: We found that following rapamycin treatment, 41.03% ± 3.268 of autophagosomes were fused with the lysosomes (RFP-tagged red puncta), compared to 13.84% ± 1.96 in the APOE4 expressing microglia (Fig. 6).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower red-only LC3 fraction indicating reduced autolysosome formation)
row.Experimental system: Stable human FLAG-APOE3- or FLAG-APOE4-expressing murine N9 microglia; transient tandem LC3-EGFP-mRFP reporter; 150 nM rapamycin for 24 h beginning 48 h after transfection; confocal imaging and puncta-area quantification. Acid-sensitive reporter behavior supports a flux/lysosomal-delivery interpretation but does not isolate fusion from acidification.

proposed.why: Same tandem LC3 reporter (red-only vs yellow puncta) readout as the other APOE3-vs-APOE4 tandem-LC3 rows: autophagic flux/autolysosome formation is B itself and A is the APOE isoform, so class 1 strength 2 like the checked lysosomal-pH reference row.

row.Finding description: Following chloroquine treatment, normalized p62 was lower in APOE4 than APOE3 microglia, 0.629 ± 0.068 versus 0.954 ± 0.059, supporting reduced autophagic flux. Effect is the ratio of the two group values printed in the quote (0.954 ± 0.059 and 0.629 ± 0.068).
row.Finding quote: However, the levels of p62 following chloroquine treatment were significantly higher in APOE3 microglia compared to APOE4 microglia (0.954 ± 0.059 and 0.629 ± 0.068, respectively).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower p62 accumulation during lysosomal blockade)
row.Experimental system: Stable human FLAG-APOE3- or FLAG-APOE4-expressing murine N9 microglia; experiment used 1 h EBSS with or without 10 µM chloroquine; p62 western blot densitometry normalized to APOE3 control. The numerical CQ comparison is not unambiguously assigned to CQ alone versus EBSS plus CQ in the supplied narrative.

row.Finding description: After 0.5 h starvation, normalized p62 remained higher in APOE4 than APOE3 microglia: 0.932 ± 0.065 versus 0.592 ± 0.012.
row.Finding quote: Moreover, the levels of p62, which is associated with the degradation steps during autophagy, decreased following amino acid starvation more rapidly in APOE3 microglia compared to APOE4 microglia (0.592 ± 0.012 and 0.592 ± 0.011 compared to 0.932 ± 0.065, and 0.889 ± 0.053, respectively).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (less p62 reduction after 0.5 h starvation)
row.Experimental system: Stable human FLAG-APOE3- or FLAG-APOE4-expressing murine N9 microglia; 0.5 h EBSS starvation; p62 western blot densitometry normalized to each line's time-zero control. p62 abundance is used as a degradation surrogate; lipid metabolism was not measured.

row.Finding description: After 100 nM rapamycin, normalized p62 was higher in APOE4 than APOE3 microglia: 1.055 ± 0.055 versus 0.777 ± 0.063, indicating less p62 reduction.
row.Finding quote: Accordingly, the LC3II/actin ratio under these conditions was 1.508 ± 0.043 and 1.522 ± 0.069 in APOE3 expressing microglia, compared to 1.171 ± 0.078 and 1.33 ± 0.112, in APOE4 expressing microglia, (Fig. 4) whereas the corresponding p62 levels were 0.777 ± 0.063 and 0.706 ± 0.079, compared to 1.055 ± 0.055 and 1.026 ± 0.063, in APOE4 expressing microglia, which did not show any change in p62 levels during the experimental time frame (Fig. 4).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (less p62 reduction with 100 nM rapamycin)
row.Experimental system: Stable human FLAG-APOE3- or FLAG-APOE4-expressing murine N9 microglia; 100 nM rapamycin for 24 h; p62 western blot densitometry normalized to each line's untreated control. p62 abundance is an autophagic-degradation surrogate; lipid mediation was not tested.

row.Finding description: Starvation-induced LC3 and p62 changes in APOE4 microglia were interpreted as weaker autophagy induction than in APOE3 microglia.
row.Finding quote: Thus, the results suggest that induction of autophagy may be also impaired in APOE4 microglia.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (weaker starvation-induced autophagy-marker responses)
row.Experimental system: Murine N9 microglia stably expressing human FLAG-APOE3 or FLAG-APOE4; amino-acid starvation in EBSS; LC3-I, LC3-II and p62 measured by western blot. No lipid-metabolism measurements or human-derived cells.

row.Finding description: Following Abeta washout, APOE4 microglia retained more fluorescent Abeta than APOE3 microglia (at 4.25 h, ~0.84 vs ~0.26 fold of control; effect is the APOE4/APOE3 ratio of remaining fluorescence), interpreted as lower Abeta degradation.
row.Finding quote: Next, we measured the rate of Aβ degradation in APOE3 compared to APOE4 cells, and as shown the degradation of Aβ was significantly higher in APOE3 expressing cells compared to APOE4 expressing microglial cells (Fig. 2B).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower apparent intracellular Aβ degradation)
row.Experimental system: Murine N9 microglia stably expressing human FLAG-APOE3 or FLAG-APOE4; loaded with 0.1 µM HiLyte 488-Aβ1–42 for 2 h, washed twice with PBS, then imaged for 2 h in Aβ-free medium; intracellular fluorescence loss used as degradation readout. Lysosomal specificity and lipid mediation were not established.

row.Finding description: Following CCCP, approximately 55% of autophagosomes in APOE4 astrocytes versus approximately 90% in APOE3 astrocytes were reported fused with lysosomes (APOE4/APOE3 = 0.61x).
row.Finding quote: Furthermore, using the tandem LC3-GFP-RFP reporter30, we found that following CCCP treatment, ~90% of autophagosomes in the APOE3 astrocytes were fused with lysosomes, compared to ~55% in the APOE4 astrocytes (Fig. 3c).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower autophagosome maturation/fusion with lysosomes after CCCP)
