row.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse APOE3/APOE4 astrocyte lines transiently expressing LC3-EGFP-mRFP; 10 μM CCCP for 4 h; dual-positive versus red-only puncta area analysis; at least 50 cells per treatment. Lipid metabolism was not measured.

row.Finding description: Chloroquine-sensitive LC3-II turnover after CCCP was lower in APOE4 than APOE3 astrocytes, indicating reduced autophagic flux.
row.Finding quote: Accordingly, APOE3 astrocytes treated with CCCP combined with chloroquine showed increased accumulation of LC3-II compared to APOE4 astrocytes, indicating higher autophagic flux30 (Fig. 3d).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower autophagic flux after mitochondrial damage)
row.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse APOE3/APOE4 astrocyte lines; 10 μM chloroquine for 48 h with or without 7.5 μM CCCP during the final 24 h; LC3-II difference with versus without chloroquine; n = 3, experimental unit unspecified.

row.Finding description: Chloroquine caused less mitochondrial p62 accumulation in APOE4 than APOE3 astrocytes, suggesting reduced lysosome-dependent cargo turnover.
row.Finding quote: As shown in Fig. 2a, increased accumulation (differences between CQ treated and untreated cells) of parkin, p62, LC3-II and ubiquitin was observed in the mitochondrial fraction of the APOE3 astrocytes following treatment, suggesting their degradation is reduced in APOE4 astrocytes.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower chloroquine-sensitive mitochondrial p62 turnover)
row.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocyte lines expressing human APOE3 or APOE4; 10 μM chloroquine for 24 h versus untreated controls; mitochondrial p62 immunoblotting normalized to AIF.

row.Finding description: Chloroquine increased parkin abundance only in APOE3 astrocytes, suggesting reduced lysosome-dependent parkin degradation in APOE4 astrocytes.
row.Finding quote: Additionally, treatment with chloroquine/MG-132 led to parkin accumulation only in the APOE3 astrocytes (Fig. 4e, f), indicating its reduced mitophagic and proteasomal degradation, respectively, in the APOE4 astrocytes.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower chloroquine-sensitive parkin degradation)
row.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse APOE3/APOE4 astrocyte lines; 10 μM chloroquine for 24 h versus untreated controls; whole-cell parkin immunoblotting.

row.Finding description: At 12 μM CCCP, p62 abundance decreased only in APOE3 astrocytes, suggesting reduced p62 degradation in APOE4 astrocytes.
row.Finding quote: In addition, 12 µM CCCP treatment reduced p62 levels only in the APOE3 astrocytes, indicating increased p62 degradation in these cells (Fig. S1b).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (less CCCP-associated p62 degradation)
row.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse APOE3/APOE4 astrocyte lines; 12 μM CCCP for 24 h versus untreated controls; p62 immunoblotting.

row.Finding description: Compared with ApoE3, ApoE4 increased cholesterol accumulation in lysosomes of PHF-treated BV2 microglia, assessed by filipin and LysoTracker imaging in 8–18 fields from three biological replicates.
row.Finding quote: ApoE4 significantly increased the accumulation of cholesterol in lysosomes of microglia treated with PHF compared to ApoE3, while treatment with capsaicin significantly decreased it (Fig. 5k, l).
row.Finding summary: (ApoE3 -> ApoE4, with PHF) -> (increased lysosomal cholesterol accumulation)
row.Experimental system: Mouse BV2 immortalized microglial cells, not non-aged human brain cells. Recombinant human ApoE3 or ApoE4, 4 μg/ml for 6 h with 10% FBS, washing and 4 h in fresh medium, then 1 μg/ml tau PHF for 24 h. Lysosomes were labeled with 50 nM LysoTracker Red for 30 min and cholesterol with filipin III; confocal imaging assessed lysosomal cholesterol accumulation.

proposed.why: Lysosomal cholesterol by cholesterol-probe/lysosome-marker colocalization is a static surrogate for cholesterol egress, the same readout as the P34 D4H*-LAMP1 rows (3/3); increased cholesterol delivery (e.g. apoE-lipoprotein uptake) is an alternative route.

row.Finding description: In the ApoE isoform treatment experiment, ApoE4 plus PHF produced more autophagosomes relative to autolysosomes, indicating impaired autophagic processing in BV2 microglia; the panel legend reports 10–12 fields from three biological replicates.
row.Finding quote: We detected increased autophagosomes (remaining yellow dots in Fig. 5i) relative to autolysosomes in microglia treated with ApoE4 in the presence of PHF, indicating impaired autophagy lysosomal pathway.
row.Finding summary: (ApoE3 -> ApoE4, with PHF) -> (increased autophagosomes relative to autolysosomes)
row.Experimental system: Mouse BV2 immortalized microglial cell line from the Cell Bank of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, not non-aged human brain cells. Recombinant human ApoE3 or ApoE4, 4 μg/ml for 6 h with 10% FBS, followed by washing, 4 h in fresh medium and 1 μg/ml tau PHF for 24 h. Fixed-cell tandem mRFP-GFP-LC3 fluorescence imaging assessed autophagosome versus autolysosome puncta. No donor age or strain background was reported.

proposed.why: Same tandem LC3 reporter (red-only vs yellow puncta) readout as the other APOE3-vs-APOE4 tandem-LC3 rows: autophagic flux/autolysosome formation is B itself and A is the APOE isoform, so class 1 strength 2 like the checked lysosomal-pH reference row.

row.Finding description: Capsaicin restored the tandem LC3 reporter pattern interpreted as autophagic processing in ApoE4-plus-PHF BV2 microglia, with 10–12 fields from three biological replicates; this tests rescue at fixed ApoE4 exposure.
row.Finding quote: Treatment with TRPV1 agonist capsaicin restored the autophagy lysosomal pathway in microglia (Fig. 5i, j).
row.Finding summary: (vehicle -> capsaicin, with ApoE4 and PHF) -> (restored autophagy lysosomal pathway)
row.Experimental system: Mouse BV2 immortalized microglial cells loaded with recombinant human ApoE4, 4 μg/ml for 6 h in 10% FBS, washed and incubated for 4 h in fresh medium. Cells received vehicle or 1 μM capsaicin for 30 min before 1 μg/ml tau PHF for 24 h. Tandem mRFP-GFP-LC3 fluorescence images assessed autophagosome and autolysosome puncta.

proposed.reason_for_description: The manipulation is the TRPV1 agonist capsaicin at fixed ApoE4 exposure, which does not act on APOE, so no class 1-4 form fits.

row.Finding description: Following Aβ42 treatment, lysosomal inhibition produced greater intracellular Aβ42 accumulation in APOE3 than isogenic APOE4 astrocytes, suggesting reduced lysosome-dependent Aβ42 degradation in APOE4 cells, although lipid mediation was not tested.
row.Finding quote: Since lysosomal activity can affect Aβ levels, we also examined lysosome-dependent degradation of Aβ42 by measuring intracellular Aβ with or without lysosomal inhibitors following Aβ42 treatment. We observed increased Aβ42 accumulation following lysosome inhibition in APOE3 astrocytes compared to APOE4 astrocytes, suggesting reduced lysosome-dependent Aβ42 degradation in APOE4 astrocytes (Figure S3D).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower inferred lysosome-dependent Aβ42 degradation in human iPSC-derived astrocytes)
row.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived astrocytes from unaffected female donor line AG09173, donor age 75, comparing parental homozygous APOE3 with CRISPR/Cas9-generated isogenic homozygous APOE4; cultured differentiated cells, with no cellular-aging intervention reported. Intracellular Aβ42 was measured after Aβ42 treatment with or without lysosomal inhibitors. Methods specify 48-hour treatment with leupeptin (50 μM), chloroquine (50 μM), and ammonium chloride (10 mM). The supplementary panel and its complete assay details were unavailable.

proposed.why: Lysosome-inhibitor-sensitive Aβ42 accumulation measures lysosome-dependent degradation (B itself) with APOE isoform as A, the same inhibitor-sensitive cargo design scored 1/2 in P29.F3/F4 and P7.F1.

row.Finding description: Adding the PPAR-γ inhibitor GW9662 abolished the Lilrb4a-knockdown-associated enhancement of Aβ uptake and degradation in APOE4 mouse microglia, with n=3 and replicate identity unspecified.
row.Finding quote: In both APOE3 and APOE4‐derived microglia, Lilrb4a knockdown enhanced Aβ phagocytosis and degradation, whereas PPAR‐γ inhibition abolished the enhancement of Aβ phagocytosis and degradation induced by Lilrb4a knockdown (Figure 4L–O).
row.Finding summary: (Lilrb4a ASO -> Lilrb4a ASO plus PPAR-γ inhibition in APOE4 microglia) -> (loss of enhanced Aβ uptake and degradation)
row.Experimental system: Primary cortical CD11b-enriched microglia from 12-month-old human APOE4 knock-in mice given intraperitoneal LPS, 3 mg/kg, 24 hours before isolation. row.Finding quote: Additionally, there was also a decrease in the colocalization of the receptors with the lysosomes in APOE4 neurons that was significant in APOER2 and VEGFR but not in the IR (APOER2 : 35.89% decrease, p < 0.0001; VEGFR: 31.30% decrease, p < 0.05), and in the recycling endosomes in all three receptors (APOER2 : 11.16% decrease, p = 0.5154; IR: 30.88% decrease, p < 0.05; VEGFR: 29.02% decrease, p < 0.05) when compared to APOE3 neurons.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower VEGFR colocalization with lysosomes)
row.Experimental system: Primary neuronal-enriched brain cultures from neonatal human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice on an α-syn-/- background; experiments generally at day 21; VEGFR2/CatD double immunofluorescence, confocal microscopy, and M1 colocalization analysis.

row.Finding description: APOE4 mouse neurons showed 20.2% lower LRP1 colocalization with lysosomes than APOE3 neurons; the legend reports 25–37 cells from 2–3 preparations per comparison.
row.Finding quote: The first pattern which was observed with LRP1, shows that lower levels of colocalization of this receptor in the early endosomes in APOE4 neurons (seen also in Fig. 5) was accompanied by lower levels of their colocalization with late endosomes (46.7% decrease, p < 0.01) and lysosomes (20.2% decrease, p < 0.05), while no difference between the genotypes was seen in the corresponding recycling endosomes.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower LRP1 colocalization with lysosomes)
row.Experimental system: Primary neuronal-enriched brain cultures from neonatal human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice on an α-syn-/- background; experiments generally at day 21; LRP1/CatD double immunofluorescence, confocal microscopy, and M1 colocalization analysis.

row.Finding description: APOE4 mouse neurons showed a reported 22.09% decrease in APOER2 late-endosome colocalization versus APOE3, but no significant difference; 25–37 cells from 2–3 preparations were reported per comparison.
row.Finding quote: This decrease in late endosomes was significant for both IR and VEGFR with a similar trend observed in APOER2 (IR: 25.80% decrease, p < 0.05; VEGFR: 47.74% decrease, p < 0.05; APOER2 : 22.09% decrease, p = 0.156).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in APOER2 late-endosome colocalization reaching statistical significance)
row.Experimental system: Primary neuronal-enriched brain cultures from neonatal human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice on an α-syn-/- background; experiments generally at day 21; APOER2/Rab7 double immunofluorescence, confocal microscopy, and M1 colocalization analysis.

row.Finding description: APOE4 mouse neurons showed 46.7% lower LRP1 colocalization with late endosomes than APOE3 neurons; the legend reports 25–37 cells from 2–3 preparations per receptor–compartment comparison.
row.Finding quote: The first pattern which was observed with LRP1, shows that lower levels of colocalization of this receptor in the early endosomes in APOE4 neurons (seen also in Fig. 5) was accompanied by lower levels of their colocalization with late endosomes (46.7% decrease, p < 0.01) and lysosomes (20.2% decrease, p < 0.05), while no difference between the genotypes was seen in the corresponding recycling endosomes.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower LRP1 colocalization with late endosomes)

row.Finding description: Across three independent experiments, one-hour recombinant apoE4 treatment increased cytosolic Cathepsin D compared with apoE3 in SH-SY5Y cells, supporting leakage from lysosomal compartments.
row.Finding quote: Analysis of microsomal and cytosolic fractions revealed that Cathepsin D levels were increased in the cytosolic fraction of rApoE4-treated cells compared to rApoE3- and non-treated cells (Fig. 5C).
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (higher cytosolic Cathepsin D in SH-SY5Y cells)
row.Experimental system: Human ATCC SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells treated in serum-free medium with 100 nM human recombinant apoE3 or apoE4 for 1 h; differential centrifugation to obtain microsomal and cytosolic fractions, followed by Cathepsin D immunoblotting; Ponceau staining used as loading control.

proposed.why: Same microsomal/cytosolic fractionation experiment as P8.F4; altered Cathepsin D sorting or fractionation carry-over is a possible but unlikely-to-invalidate route, so both halves get strength 3.

row.Finding description: Across three experiments, recombinant apoE4 reduced Cathepsin D–Lamp-2 colocalization relative to the apoE3 condition in human primary cortical neurons, suggesting reduced lysosomal retention of Cathepsin D.
row.Finding quote: As seen in Fig. 5E, and in agreement with the results found with SH-SY5Y cells (Fig. 5A), rApoE4-treated neurons showed reduced co-localization between Lamp-2 and Cathepsin D suggesting lower levels of Capthesin D in the lysosomes.
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (reduced Cathepsin D–Lamp-2 colocalization in human primary cortical neurons)
row.Experimental system: Human primary cortical neurons derived from embryonic cortical tissue at 6–11 weeks post-conception, obtained after elective abortions from healthy pregnant women without known AD pathology; cultured for 10 days before treatment; 100 nM human recombinant apoE3 or apoE4 for 1 h; Cathepsin D and Lamp-2 immunocytochemistry with confocal microscopy.

row.Finding description: Across three experiments, recombinant apoE4 produced more diffuse Lamp-2 and Cathepsin D staining and reduced their colocalization compared with apoE3 in SH-SY5Y cells, indicating impaired lysosomal retention without testing lipid-metabolism mediation.
row.Finding quote: This pattern was not changed by treatment with rApoE3. However, treatment with rApoE4 resulted in decreased staining of both Lamp-2 and Cathepsin D with more diffuse patterns. In addition, rApoE4 exposure resulted in reduced co-localization between Cathepsin D and Lamp-2 compared to rApoE3-treated and control cells (Fig. 5A).
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (more diffuse lysosomal-marker staining and reduced Cathepsin D–Lamp-2 colocalization in SH-SY5Y cells)
row.Experimental system: Human SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells obtained from ATCC; serum-free treatment with 100 nM human recombinant apoE3 or apoE4, described as lipid-free in the Discussion; Cathepsin D and Lamp-2 immunocytochemistry with confocal microscopy. Treatment duration conflicts: Results states 5 h, whereas the Fig 5A legend states 1 h.

row.Finding description: Across three independent experiments, microsomal Cathepsin D was lower after one-hour recombinant apoE4 treatment than after apoE3 treatment in SH-SY5Y cells.
row.Finding quote: In rApoE3 treated cells, the levels of Cathepsin D were instead increased in the microsomal fraction compared to rApoE4 treated and control cells.
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4) -> (lower microsomal Cathepsin D in SH-SY5Y cells)
row.Experimental system: Human ATCC SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells treated with 100 nM human recombinant apoE3 or apoE4 in serum-free medium for 1 h; microsomal fraction collected by 100,000×g centrifugation and analyzed by Cathepsin D immunoblotting; Ponceau staining used as loading control.

row.Finding description: In fibrillar Aβ-challenged APOE4/4 iMG, 10 μM GNE-317 reversed lysosomal accumulation measured by LysoTracker staining in three replicate wells per condition while also reducing lipid droplet accumulation.
row.Finding quote: In addition, PI3K inhibition with GNE-317 reversed the lysosomal accumulation and inflammatory cytokine secretion observed in iMGs with high concentrations of LDs (Extended Data Fig. 7e,f).
row.Finding summary: (GNE-317 treatment in fAβ-challenged APOE4/4 iMG) -> (reduced LysoTracker-defined lysosomal accumulation)
row.Experimental system: Human APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia; untreated, 5 μM Aβ-treated, and Aβ plus 10 μM GNE-317 conditions over 24 h; the relevant rescue comparison is Aβ plus GNE-317 versus Aβ alone; LysoTracker staining.

proposed.why: GNE-317 inhibits PI3K, which regulates lysosome biogenesis through mTORC1/TFEB directly, a known route to the LysoTracker change other than via APOE4 lipid effects, so strength 4.
proposed.reason_for_description: GNE-317 is a PI3K inhibitor applied within the APOE4/4 genotype and does not act on APOE, so the perturbation is neither A nor a surrogate A'.

row.Finding description: Lipid droplet-containing APOE4/4 iMG showed greater lysosomal accumulation. Fig. 3s measured the percentage of LysoTracker-positive iMG among cells with and without lipid droplets, using three replicate wells per condition.
row.Finding quote: In accordance with these RNA-seq results, phenotypic measurements of LD-containing APOE4/4 iMGs indicate that they are dysfunctional in phagocytosis, accumulate lysosomes and secrete inflammation-associated chemokines as measured in the cell culture media (Fig. 3r,s and Extended Data Fig. 6f,g,i).
row.Finding summary: A greater percentage of lipid droplet-positive APOE4/4 iMG were LysoTracker-positive than lipid droplet-negative iMG.
row.Experimental system: Human APOE4/4 iPSC-derived microglia in the fibrillar Aβ assay. Fig. 3s groups cells by lipid droplet presence or absence. The live-imaging protocol specifies 5 μM fibrillar Aβ for 24 h before staining.

proposed.reason_for_description: Cells within one APOE4/4 genotype are stratified by lipid-droplet presence, an observational within-genotype comparison that does not vary APOE, so it fits none of classes 1-4.

row.Finding description: Recombinant ApoE4 increased ABCA1 colocalization with LAMP2 compared with ApoE3 in human HeLa cells, indicating altered localization rather than directly measured lysosomal function.
row.Finding quote: Greater colocalization of ABCA1 with the late endosome marker LAMP2 and lower colocalization with the recycling endosome marker Rab11 were observed in cells treated with rApoE4 compared with rApoE3 ( Fig. 2 ).
row.Finding summary: (rApoE3 -> rApoE4) -> (greater ABCA1 colocalization with LAMP2)
row.Experimental system: Human HeLa cells, not brain cells, stably expressing GFP-tagged ABCA1; 0.2 μM recombinant ApoE3 or ApoE4 for 30 minutes; confocal imaging with LAMP2 immunostaining.

proposed.why: Cargo or receptor colocalization with late endosomes/lysosomes reflects upstream endosomal sorting and recycling, a known route that changes it without any change in lysosomal function, so strength 4 (harmonized across all cargo-colocalization rows).

row.Finding description: TOFA treatment from embryos produced no apparent change in APOE4-associated neuronal lysosomal abnormalities relative to DMSO in young adult C. elegans (no significant difference reported, although no statistical test was supplied).
row.Finding quote: We treated the APOE4; PVD::GFP strain with TOFA starting at the embryo stage and found that TOFA partially rescued APOE4-induced PVD neurodegeneration (Fig. 5G,H) without apparently altering APOE4-induced lysosomal defects (Fig. EV5A).
row.Finding summary: (DMSO -> TOFA in APOE4-expressing C. elegans) -> (no change in neuronal lysosomal abnormalities)
row.Experimental system: C. elegans expressing human APOE4 pan-neuronally through vxIs824 [rab-3p::ND18ApoE4::unc-54 3’UTR + myo-2p::mCherry::unc-54 3’UTR], with neuronal lysosomal membrane reporter ceIs56 [unc-129p::ctns-1::mCherry + nlp-21p::Venus + ttx-3p::RFP]; DMSO or TOFA treatment beginning at the embryo stage, assessed at the young adult stage by confocal fluorescence imaging. The lysosomal endpoint is reporter-defined morphology, a surrogate for function. No APOE3 comparison or direct lysosomal functional assay is reported for this result.

proposed.why: TOFA is a lipid-synthesis drug given within one APOE4 genotype with no APOE3 comparison, which the brief defines as class 5, not class 4.
proposed.reason_for_description: TOFA is an acetyl-CoA carboxylase (lipid-synthesis) inhibitor given within APOE4-expressing worms without an APOE3 arm, so APOE is not varied and the perturbation is not a surrogate A'.

row.Finding description: APOE4 acidic organelles were significantly more alkaline than APOE3 organelles by 0.14 pH units, although both remained within the reported standard lysosomal pH range.
row.Finding quote: We found that both APOE3 and APOE4 astrocytes had standard lysosomal-related pH, with a minimal but significant difference of 0.14 pH units between genotypes, APOE4 lysosomes being more alkaline (Fig. 4g).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher acidic-organelle pH)
row.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE3 or APOE4; donor age unspecified and sex identity lost; 10% FBS, ratiometric LysoSensor Yellow/Blue DND-160 fluorometry calibrated with monensin and nigericin.

row.Finding description: APOE4 astrocytes had a larger perinuclear lysosome fraction, reported at 10 μm from the nuclear center as 37% versus 21% in APOE3 cells; N was three, with 30–40 cells quantified.
row.Finding quote: Specifically, 37% of lysosomes are placed at 10 μm from the center of the nucleus in APOE4 cells, as compared to 21% in APOE3 astrocytes.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (greater perinuclear accumulation of LAMP1-positive compartments)
row.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE3 or APOE4; donor age unspecified and sex identity lost; LAMP1 immunofluorescence, confocal microscopy, and Imaris distance analysis of vesicles larger than 0.5 μm relative to the nuclear center.

row.Finding description: In APOE4 astrocytes, Ned-19 strongly reduced ATP-evoked cytosolic calcium responses, bringing them to a magnitude similar to APOE3 responses.
row.Finding quote: Interestingly, Ned-19 greatly reduced Ca2+ responses in APOE4 astrocytes, such that purinergic-mediated Ca2+ responses in the presence of Ned-19 were of similar magnitude in both cell types.
row.Finding summary: (NAADP-pathway inhibition in APOE4 astrocytes) -> (lower acidic-store-dependent ATP-evoked calcium responses)
row.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE3 or APOE4, provided by Holtzman; donor age unspecified and sex identity lost through aneuploidy; 10% FBS, 100 μM Ned-19 for 20 minutes versus 0.1% DMSO, 100 μM ATP, fura-2/AM imaging.

proposed.why: Ned-19 is a drug applied within APOE4 cells and does not act on APOE, so the brief puts it in class 5; acidic-store calcium is a loose readout of lysosome function.
proposed.reason_for_description: Class 5: Ned-19, an NAADP-pathway inhibitor, was applied within APOE4 astrocytes, so APOE itself was not varied and the readout is ATP-evoked cytosolic calcium rather than lysosome function.

row.Finding description: GPN-induced cytosolic calcium AUC was greater in APOE4 than APOE3 astrocytes, supporting greater calcium content in lysosome-enriched acidic stores.
row.Finding quote: The results showed greater AUC in APOE4 cells (Fig. 4d), supporting a higher concentration of lysosomal-related Ca2+ in APOE4 cells, as compared to APOE3.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (greater GPN-releasable acidic-store calcium)
row.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE3 or APOE4; donor age unspecified and sex identity lost; 10% FBS, 200 μM GPN, fura-2/AM cytosolic calcium AUC used to infer acidic-store calcium content.

row.Finding description: Bafilomycin reduced ATP-evoked calcium responses in APOE4 astrocytes, supporting dependence of their hyperactivity on acidic stores.
row.Finding quote: Accordingly, bafilomycin A1 reduced the ATP-induced Ca2+ release in APOE4 astrocytes, confirming the dependence of these Ca2+ responses on acidic stores (Fig. 4e).
row.Finding summary: (V-ATPase inhibition in APOE4 astrocytes) -> (lower ATP-evoked calcium responses)
row.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE4; donor age unspecified and sex identity lost; 10% FBS, 2 μM bafilomycin A1 for 20 minutes versus DMSO, 100 μM ATP, fura-2/AM imaging.

proposed.why: Bafilomycin is a drug applied within APOE4 cells and does not act on APOE, so the brief puts it in class 5; matched to the APOE3 arm (P5.F12).
proposed.reason_for_description: Class 5: bafilomycin A1 was applied within APOE4 astrocytes, so APOE itself was not varied and the readout is ATP-evoked cytosolic calcium rather than lysosome function.

row.Finding description: APOE4 astrocytes had higher expression of lysosomal V-ATPase subunit V0D1 than APOE3 astrocytes.
row.Finding quote: Indeed, the expression of V-ATPase subunit V0D1, which is highly expressed in astrocytes [61], was higher in APOE4 cells than in APOE3 cells (Fig. 4f).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher V-ATPase subunit V0D1 protein expression)
row.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE3 or APOE4; donor age unspecified and sex identity lost; V0D1 western blot normalized to β-actin.

row.Finding description: Bafilomycin increased basal cytosolic calcium in APOE4 astrocytes from 0.30 ± 0.01 to 0.40 ± 0.05 fluorescence-ratio units.
row.Finding quote: Bafilomycin A1 increased basal cytoplasmic Ca2+ concentration in APOE4 astrocytes to 0.40 ± 0.05 (control values of astrocytes treated with vehicle were 0.30 ± 0.01; p-value = 0.05), whereas there was no effect on non-stimulated intracellular Ca2+ levels in APOE3 (0.44 ± 0.08 for cells treated with bafilomycin A1 compared to 0.39 ± 0.02 of cells treated with vehicle).
row.Finding summary: (V-ATPase inhibition in APOE4 astrocytes) -> (higher basal cytosolic calcium)
row.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE4; donor age unspecified and sex identity lost; 10% FBS, 2 μM bafilomycin A1 for 20 minutes versus DMSO, basal fura-2/AM fluorescence ratio.

proposed.why: Bafilomycin is a drug applied within APOE4 cells and does not act on APOE, so the brief puts it in class 5; matched to the APOE3 arm (P5.F13).
proposed.reason_for_description: Class 5: bafilomycin A1 was applied within APOE4 astrocytes, so APOE itself was not varied and the readout is basal cytosolic calcium rather than lysosome function.

row.Finding description: None of the 19 identified lysosomal lipids showed a significant APOE4-versus-APOE3 difference after FDR correction, despite mixed phospholipid changes and increased carnitine.
row.Finding quote: We could identify 19 lipids: 10 phosphatidylcholines (6 increased, 4 decreased), 5 phosphatidylethanolamine (2 increased, 3 decreased), 2 lysophosphatidylcholine (2 decreased), 1 lysophosphatidylethanolamine (decreased), and 1 carnitine (increased) (Fig. 8d). However, multi t-test analysis corrected by a false discovery rate (FDR) of these 19 FC values gave no statistically significant differences (q-value < 0.05).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no significant change in individual identified lysosomal lipids after FDR correction)
row.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE3 or APOE4; donor age unspecified and sex identity lost; isolated lysosomal membrane lipidomics, accurate-mass lipid identification, APOE4/APOE3 fold changes, and multiple t-tests with 5% FDR correction.

row.Finding description: Removing extracellular lipids produced no significant difference in GPN-estimated acidic-store calcium content in APOE4 astrocytes.
row.Finding quote: Surprisingly, measurement of Ca2+ stored inside acidic organelles using the GPN-elicited depletion showed no increased Ca2+ loading in APOE3 cells kept in KH (Fig. 7b) compared to APOE3 astrocytes kept in the presence of FBS, whereas, as expected, no difference was observed between the two conditions in APOE4 astrocytes (Fig. 7c).
row.Finding summary: (FBS-containing medium -> lipid-free KH in APOE4 astrocytes) -> (no change in acidic-store calcium content)
row.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE4; donor age unspecified and sex identity lost; acute lipid-free Krebs medium versus DMEM with FBS, 200 μM GPN, fura-2/AM cytosolic calcium AUC.

proposed.why: Lipid removal within APOE4 cells does not act on APOE, and the brief puts lipid manipulations within one genotype in class 5.
proposed.reason_for_description: Class 5: extracellular lipids were removed within APOE4 astrocytes, so APOE itself was not varied and the readout is GPN-released acidic-store calcium rather than lysosome function.

row.Finding description: Analysis of 35 lysosomal membrane lipids selected by VIP > 1 found significant APOE4-versus-APOE3 differences, with identified lipid species changing in both directions.
row.Finding quote: In lysosomal membranes, there were 35 lipids with VIP > 1 in the APOE4 vs APOE3. ANOVA analysis with a Tukey correction post-test of the intensity (peak values) of these 35 metabolites revealed significant differences due to the APOE phenotype with a p-value < 0.05, confirming, again, that expression of APOE4 alters the lipidome of lysosomes. We then proceeded to identification of the particular metabolites and calculation of their fold change (FC) in APOE4 vs APOE3 astrocytes. We could identify 19 lipids: 10 phosphatidylcholines (6 increased, 4 decreased), 5 phosphatidylethanolamine (2 increased, 3 decreased), 2 lysophosphatidylcholine (2 decreased), 1 lysophosphatidylethanolamine (decreased), and 1 carnitine (increased) (Fig. 8d).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (mixed changes in selected lysosomal membrane lipids)
row.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE3 or APOE4; donor age unspecified and sex identity lost; isolated lysosomal membrane untargeted lipidomics, VIP selection, and ANOVA with Tukey correction.

row.Finding description: Lysosomal membrane lipid profiles separated APOE4 from APOE3 astrocytes by PLS-DA, providing a compositional surrogate rather than a direct measure of impaired lysosomal function.
row.Finding quote: The multivariate analysis PLS-DA revealed that the lipids of lysosomal membranes (Fig. 8b) and whole-membranes (Fig. 8c) clustered independently in APOE3 and APOE4 genotypes.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (altered lysosomal membrane lipid composition)
row.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE3 or APOE4; donor age unspecified and sex identity lost; lysosomes isolated by density gradients, membranes separated after freeze–thaw disruption, untargeted mass-spectrometry lipidomics and PLS-DA.

row.Finding description: In the APOE3 control arm, bafilomycin produced no significant difference in ATP-evoked calcium responses.
row.Finding quote: In contrast, bafilomycin A1 did not change purinergic-induced Ca2+ responses in APOE3 astrocytes.
row.Finding summary: (V-ATPase inhibition in APOE3 astrocytes) -> (no change in ATP-evoked calcium responses)
row.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE3, studied alongside APOE4 cells; donor age unspecified; 10% FBS, 2 μM bafilomycin A1 for 20 minutes versus DMSO, 100 μM ATP, fura-2/AM imaging.

proposed.why: Bafilomycin is a drug applied within APOE3 cells and does not act on APOE, so the brief puts it in class 5; matched to the APOE4 arm (P5.F5).
proposed.reason_for_description: Class 5: bafilomycin A1 was applied within APOE3 astrocytes, so APOE itself was not varied and the readout is ATP-evoked cytosolic calcium rather than lysosome function.

row.Finding description: In the APOE3 control arm, bafilomycin produced no significant difference in basal cytosolic calcium, with values of 0.44 ± 0.08 versus 0.39 ± 0.02.
row.Finding quote: Bafilomycin A1 increased basal cytoplasmic Ca2+ concentration in APOE4 astrocytes to 0.40 ± 0.05 (control values of astrocytes treated with vehicle were 0.30 ± 0.01; p-value = 0.05), whereas there was no effect on non-stimulated intracellular Ca2+ levels in APOE3 (0.44 ± 0.08 for cells treated with bafilomycin A1 compared to 0.39 ± 0.02 of cells treated with vehicle).
row.Finding summary: (V-ATPase inhibition in APOE3 astrocytes) -> (no change in basal cytosolic calcium)
row.Experimental system: Immortalized mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE3, studied alongside APOE4 cells; donor age unspecified; 10% FBS, 2 μM bafilomycin A1 for 20 minutes versus DMSO, basal fura-2/AM fluorescence ratio.

proposed.why: Bafilomycin is a drug applied within APOE3 cells and does not act on APOE, so the brief puts it in class 5; matched to the APOE4 arm (P5.F7).
proposed.reason_for_description: Class 5: bafilomycin A1 was applied within APOE3 astrocytes, so APOE itself was not varied and the readout is basal cytosolic calcium rather than lysosome function.

row.Finding description: Magic Red Cathepsin B quantification across three independent experiments showed reduced lysosomal cathepsin-dependent proteolysis in APOE4 versus APOE3 Neuro-2a cells (APOE3 normalized to 1.0, APOE4 ~0.75).
row.Finding quote: We found that the HsAPOE4-expressing cells exhibited significantly decreased MR-CTSB proteolysis compared to HsAPOE3-expressing cells, in line with their decreased lysosomal acidity (Figure 1F,G).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower lysosomal cathepsin B substrate cleavage)
row.Experimental system: Murine male Neuro-2a cells expressing genomic human APOE3 or APOE4; live-cell Magic Red Cathepsin B fluorescence microscopy.

row.Finding description: Across three independent differentiations, APOE4 human iPSC-derived neurons had lower LAMP1-proximal LGALS3BP PLA signal than isogenic APOE3 neurons.
row.Finding quote: In concordance with our observations in Neuro-2a cells, we found that APOE4 iPSC-derived neurons harbored less lysosomal LGALS3BP and more lysosomal TMED5 compared to their APOE3 counterparts (Figure 6B,C).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower lysosomal LGALS3BP PLA signal)
row.Experimental system: Human female APOE4 iPSCs and isogenic APOE3 iPSCs differentiated into mixed neuronal cultures including GABAergic interneurons; DIV49; LAMP1-LGALS3BP proximity ligation assay.

proposed.why: Lysosomal content of a cargo protein can change through altered sorting or delivery rather than impaired lysosome function; matched to the same LGALS3BP/TMED5 readouts in P19.F5 and P19.F6.

row.Finding description: FCCP increased the acidic mtKeima response in both genotypes, but the response was stronger in APOE3 than APOE4 cells across three independent experiments.
row.Finding quote: While FCCP triggered mitophagy in both HsAPOE3- and HsAPOE4-expressing cells, its induction was stronger in the HsAPOE3-expressing cells (Figure 1I,J).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (weaker FCCP-induced acidic mitochondrial mtKeima response)
row.Experimental system: Murine male Neuro-2a cells expressing human APOE3 or APOE4 and mtKeima; 10 µM FCCP; legend specifies one-hour treatment, whereas Methods specify 30 minutes before imaging; genotype-normalized ratios.

row.Finding description: Adding bafilomycin A1 to FCCP abrogated the APOE3-versus-APOE4 mtKeima difference across three independent experiments; a comparison-specific significance value was not reported.
row.Finding quote: While BafA1 as expected reduced the acidic mtKeima signal, it intriguingly also abrogated the difference between HsAPOE3- and HsAPOE4-expressing cells (Figure 1I), suggesting that mitophagic defects could be attributed to defective lysosomal acidification.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4, FCCP plus BafA1) -> (no change in acidic mitochondrial mtKeima signal)
row.Experimental system: Murine male Neuro-2a cells expressing human APOE3 or APOE4 and mtKeima; combined 10 µM FCCP and 200 nM bafilomycin A1; three independent imaging experiments.

row.Finding description: Conventional immunofluorescence across three independent experiments found no observable APOE4-versus-APOE3 difference in LGALS3BP intensity within CTSD-positive human neuronal lysosomes.
row.Finding quote: While we could not observe differences in lysosomal LGALS3BP localization by this approach (Fig. S6B-C), we could observe a slight increase in lysosomal TMED5 immunoreactivity and colocalization (Fig. S6D-E).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in LGALS3BP intensity within CTSD-positive lysosomes)
row.Experimental system: Human female APOE4 and isogenic APOE3 iPSC-derived mixed neurons at DIV49; LGALS3BP and CTSD immunofluorescence; lysosomal LGALS3BP intensity; five images from three independent experiments.

row.Finding description: Across three independent experiments, APOE4 human neurons showed a slight increase in TMED5 immunoreactivity within CTSD-positive lysosomes relative to APOE3 neurons.
row.Finding quote: While we could not observe differences in lysosomal LGALS3BP localization by this approach (Fig. S6B-C), we could observe a slight increase in lysosomal TMED5 immunoreactivity and colocalization (Fig. S6D-E).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (slightly higher TMED5 intensity within CTSD-positive lysosomes)
row.Experimental system: Human female APOE4 and isogenic APOE3 iPSC-derived mixed neurons at DIV49; TMED5 intensity within CTSD-positive lysosomes; five images from three independent experiments.

row.Finding description: Across three independent experiments, APOE4-expressing Neuro-2a cells had significantly lower LysoTracker staining than APOE3-expressing cells.
row.Finding quote: We found that the LysoTracker intensity was significantly reduced in HsAPOE4-expressing cells (Figure 1A,B), suggesting either endolysosomal alkalinization or a reduction in endolysosomal density.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower acidic-endolysosomal LysoTracker signal)
row.Experimental system: Murine male Neuro-2a neuroblastoma cells carrying the human APOE3 or APOE4 genomic locus; endogenous mouse Apoe intact; live-cell LysoTracker assay, 30-minute loading.

row.Finding description: Basal mtKeima measurements across three independent experiments indicated modestly impaired mitophagy in APOE4 versus APOE3 Neuro-2a cells.
row.Finding quote: Under basal conditions, we observed a modest impairment of mitophagy in HsAPOE4 cells (Figure 1H).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower basal acidic mitochondrial mtKeima signal)
row.Experimental system: Murine male Neuro-2a cells expressing human APOE3 or APOE4 and transient mtKeima; basal live-cell ratiometric imaging; individual mitochondria sampled across three experiments.

row.Finding description: LC3 immunoblotting contributed to the finding that autophagy remained generally functional while basal autophagy was slightly dampened in APOE4 cells.
row.Finding quote: Autophagy appeared generally functional in these cells, despite the basal autophagy being slightly dampened in HsAPOE4 cells (Fig. S1D-F).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (slightly dampened basal autophagy with generally retained autophagic function)
row.Experimental system: Murine male Neuro-2a cells expressing human APOE3 or APOE4; representative LC3-I and LC3-II western blot.

proposed.why: Steady-state LC3 immunoblot in APOE4 vs APOE3 cells, matched to the same readout in P11.F3 and P11.F4.

row.Finding description: Both APOE3 and APOE4 Neuro-2a cells showed lysosome-autophagosome fusion after three hours of starvation and bafilomycin treatment; no quantitative genotype difference was reported.
row.Finding quote: Immunofluorescence of LAMP1 and LC3 shows lysosome-autophagosome fusion in both HsAPOE3 and HsAPOE4 Neuro-2a cells following 3 h HBSS starvation and BafA1 treatment.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lysosome-autophagosome fusion remains observable)
row.Experimental system: Murine male Neuro-2a cells expressing human APOE3 or APOE4; three-hour HBSS starvation and bafilomycin A1 treatment; LAMP1 and LC3 immunofluorescence.

row.Finding description: LAMP1 immunostaining showed that lysosomal density was not decreased in APOE4 relative to APOE3 Neuro-2a cells.
row.Finding quote: We therefore stained the cells for the lysosomal membrane marker LAMP1, finding that the lysosomal density was not decreased in HsAPOE4 cells (Fig. S1B-C).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no decrease in LAMP1-based lysosomal density)
row.Experimental system: Murine male Neuro-2a cells expressing human APOE3 or APOE4; LAMP1 immunofluorescence and Fiji puncta identification.

row.Finding description: Lysosome-targeted calcium-sensor imaging across three independent experiments found comparable lysosomal calcium levels in APOE3 and APOE4 cells, without a reported significant difference.
row.Finding quote: Using GPN to release lysosomal calcium [61], we found lysosomal calcium levels to be comparable between HsAPOE3 and HsAPOE4-expressing cells (Fig. S1G-L), particularly after correcting for lysosomal density (Fig. S1M).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in estimated lysosomal calcium levels)
row.Experimental system: Murine male Neuro-2a cells expressing human APOE3 or APOE4; LAMP2-GCaMP6s sensor expressed for 48 hours; calcium-free bath; sequential 200 µM GPN and 4 µM ionomycin.

row.Finding description: APOE4 astrocytes had lower LysoTracker fluorescence than APOE3 astrocytes, interpreted as impaired lysosomal activity or acidity although this assay did not provide calibrated lysosomal pH.
row.Finding quote: Moreover, APOE3-expressing astrocytes showed higher lysosomal activity as indicated by higher lysotracker signal compared to APOE4-expressing cells (Fig. 4D).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower LysoTracker fluorescence in astrocytes)
row.Experimental system: Human APOE-expressing astrocytes of unspecified derivation and age; 60 nM LysoTracker Deep Red for 30 min at 37 °C; washed and trypsinized cells analyzed by flow cytometry; ratio paired t-test.

proposed.why: LysoTracker intensity reflects lysosome number as well as acidity, so it is a surrogate with a possible alternative route; matched to the same readout in P19.F7.

row.Finding description: Untreated APOE4 astrocytes had higher p62 levels than APOE3 astrocytes, consistent with impaired autophagic degradation but not establishing flux or a lipid-mediated mechanism.
row.Finding quote: As shown in Fig. 3A, the levels of p62 were significantly higher in APOE4-expressing cells, yet α-synuclein treatment increased the levels of p62 in the APOE3 but not in APOE4 cells in which the levels of p62 were high to begin with.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher basal p62 in astrocytes)
row.Experimental system: Human APOE3- and APOE4-expressing astrocytes previously described in reference 23; derivation, age and genetic matching unspecified; untreated comparison within a 2 h α-synuclein experiment; p62 immunoblot normalized to actin.
row.Data location: Fig. 3 p62 quantification (labelled panel B in the figure image; the text cites Fig. 3A), control APOE3 vs APOE4

proposed.why: Basal p62 can rise through transcriptional induction as well as impaired degradation, so 'strong' overstates it; matched to the other steady-state autophagy markers (P11.F3-F7).

row.Finding description: APOE4 astrocytes had significantly lower basal LC3-II than APOE3 astrocytes (the quantified panel plots the LC3-II/LC3-I ratio as % of APOE3 control), consistent with altered autophagy although steady-state LC3 alone does not establish flux.
row.Finding quote: However, the levels of LC3-II were significantly lower in APOE4 compared to APOE3-expressing astrocytes, and α-synuclein treatment had no effect on LC3-II levels in APOE4 astrocytes.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower basal LC3-II in astrocytes)
row.Experimental system: Human APOE-expressing astrocytes of unspecified derivation and age; untreated genotype comparison within a 2 h α-synuclein experiment; LC3 immunoblot normalized to actin.
row.Data location: Fig. 3 LC3 quantification (labelled panel A in the figure image, LC3-II/LC3-I ratio; the text cites Fig. 3B), control APOE3 vs APOE4

row.Finding description: APOE4 astrocytes had a significantly lower LC3-II/LC3-I ratio than APOE3 astrocytes, consistent with altered autophagy but not independently establishing flux.
row.Finding quote: The LC3-II/LC3-I ratio was significantly higher in APOE3 compared to APOE4-expressing astrocytes.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower LC3-II/LC3-I ratio)
row.Experimental system: Human APOE-expressing astrocytes of unspecified derivation and age; genotype comparison in the 24 h MPP+/rapamycin experiment; LC3 immunoblot and LC3-II/LC3-I ratio.

row.Finding description: Rapamycin-associated reduction of MPP+-elevated p62 was described as more pronounced in APOE3 than APOE4 astrocytes, without a reported genotype-by-rescue interaction test.
row.Finding quote: Combined treatment of MPP+ and rapamycin reduced p62 levels compared to MPP+ treatment alone in both APOE3 and APOE4-expressing astrocytes, with more pronounced effect on APOE3-expressing cells.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (less pronounced rapamycin-associated reduction of MPP+-elevated p62)
row.Experimental system: Human APOE-expressing astrocytes of unspecified derivation and age; 0.2 mM MPP+ with or without 100 nM rapamycin for 24 h; genotype comparison of p62 response by immunoblot.
row.Data location: Fig. 7B, genotype difference in p62 rescue

row.Finding description: α-Synuclein increased p62 in APOE3 astrocytes but produced no significant change in APOE4 astrocytes with already elevated p62, indicating different genotype-associated responses.
row.Finding quote: As shown in Fig. 3A, the levels of p62 were significantly higher in APOE4-expressing cells, yet α-synuclein treatment increased the levels of p62 in the APOE3 but not in APOE4 cells in which the levels of p62 were high to begin with.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (loss of the α-synuclein-associated increase in p62)
row.Experimental system: Human APOE3- and APOE4-expressing astrocytes, control versus 0.5 μM α-synuclein for 2 h within each genotype; p62 immunoblot normalized to actin. The paper does not specify a vehicle.
row.Data location: Fig. 3 p62 quantification (labelled panel B in the figure image; the text cites Fig. 3A), alpha-synuclein response within each genotype

row.Finding description: α-Synuclein significantly reduced LC3-II in APOE3 astrocytes but produced no significant change in APOE4 astrocytes, which already had lower LC3-II.
row.Finding quote: As shown in Fig. 3B, α-synuclein treatment significantly reduced the levels of LC3-II in APOE3-expressing astrocytes. However, the levels of LC3-II were significantly lower in APOE4 compared to APOE3-expressing astrocytes, and α-synuclein treatment had no effect on LC3-II levels in APOE4 astrocytes.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (loss of the α-synuclein-associated decrease in LC3-II)
row.Experimental system: Human APOE3- and APOE4-expressing astrocytes, control versus 0.5 μM α-synuclein for 2 h within each genotype; LC3 immunoblot normalized to actin. The paper does not specify a vehicle.
row.Data location: Fig. 3 LC3 quantification (labelled panel A in the figure image, LC3-II/LC3-I ratio; the text cites Fig. 3B), alpha-synuclein response within each genotype

row.Finding description: Combined lysosomal and proteasomal inhibition (BafA1 + MG-132, 3 h) changed far fewer proteins significantly in APOE4 than APOE3 neurons (Fig 4E: n=14 vs n=479 proteins at adj. p<0.05 and |Log2FC|>0.58), suggesting reduced baseline clearance through the jointly tested pathways.
row.Finding quote: In contrast, simultaneous inhibition of proteasomal and lysosomal protein clearance synergistically resulted in protein accumulation in APOE3 cells beyond what can be expected of additive clearance inhibition, while protein accumulation was much less evident in APOE4 neurons (Figures 4E, S4A).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (less additional protein accumulation after combined lysosomal/proteasomal blockade; baseline clearance impairment inferred)
row.Experimental system: Human female-donor isogenic APOE3/APOE3 and APOE4/APOE4 iPSC-derived mixed neuronal cultures at DIV49; donor had AD; 3-hour treatment with 200 nM bafilomycin A1 plus 10 μM MG-132 versus DMSO; housekeeping-normalized mass-spectrometric protein abundance.

row.Finding description: Proteomic PC2 responses showed accumulation of clearance-sensitive proteins after combined inhibition in APOE3 neurons, with an attenuated response in APOE4 neurons.
row.Finding quote: Accordingly, while high PC2-scoring proteins reproducibly accumulated in APOE3 neurons upon blocking lysosomal and proteasomal degradation, the same proteins appeared resilient to clearance inhibition in APOE4 neurons (Figures 4G).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (attenuated proteomic response to combined clearance blockade)
row.Experimental system: Human female-donor isogenic APOE3/APOE3 and APOE4/APOE4 iPSC-derived mixed neurons at DIV49; donor had AD; 3-hour lysosomal/proteasomal inhibitor treatments; batch-corrected mass-spectrometric protein abundance summarized by PCA PC2.

row.Finding description: Lysosomal inhibition alone (BafA1, 3 h) produced few significantly changed proteins in either genotype (Fig 4E: n=7 in APOE3, n=2 in APOE4), which the authors describe as similar numbers; no statistical test of the genotype difference is reported.
row.Finding quote: Each treatment individually had a modest impact on the proteome with a similar number of impacted proteins in both the APOE3 and APOE4 neurons (Figure S4A, Table S6).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (similar numbers of proteins responding to lysosomal inhibition)
row.Experimental system: Human female-donor isogenic APOE3/APOE3 and APOE4/APOE4 iPSC-derived mixed neurons at DIV49; donor had AD; 200 nM bafilomycin A1 for 3 hours versus DMSO; housekeeping-normalized mass-spectrometric protein-abundance responses.
row.Data location: Fig 4E, BafA1 bars (text also cites Supplementary Fig S4A, not available)

row.Finding description: PCA of clearance-inhibition proteomics showed a clearance-blockade response in APOE3 neurons that was attenuated in APOE4 neurons, indirectly suggesting baseline clearance impairment.
row.Finding quote: We performed a principal component analysis (PCA) to visualize differential effects of clearance inhibitors on the neuronal proteome (Figures S4B–C). PC1 explained 68.4% of the observed variance (Figure S4B) and was primarily associated with the APOE genotype, while PC2 (8.4% of variance) was most associated with clearance blockade. Accordingly, while high PC2-scoring proteins reproducibly accumulated in APOE3 neurons upon blocking lysosomal and proteasomal degradation, the same proteins appeared resilient to clearance inhibition in APOE4 neurons (Figures 4G).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (attenuated proteomic response to clearance blockade)
row.Experimental system: Human female-donor isogenic APOE3/APOE3 and APOE4/APOE4 iPSC-derived mixed neurons at DIV49; donor had AD; 3-hour bafilomycin A1, MG-132, combined treatment, or DMSO; PCA of batch-corrected proteomic intensities.

row.Finding description: Several proteins that accumulated after combined clearance blockade in APOE3 neurons were already elevated at APOE4 baseline, including CALM1, CAMKV and MAPT (Fig 4H), indirectly implicating impaired clearance; the text also names APP, but in Fig 4H APOE4 baseline APP sits near the APOE3 control level.
row.Finding quote: By analyzing the clearance-sensitive proteome, we found that several of the proteins accumulating by clearance blockade in APOE3 neurons were elevated at baseline in the APOE4 context (Figure 4H, S4D). This particularly affected synaptic proteins (CALM1, CAMKV), but also extended to the central AD hallmark proteins amyloid precursor protein (APP) and Tau (MAPT; Figure 4H).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher baseline abundance of proteins sensitive to combined clearance blockade)
row.Experimental system: Human female-donor isogenic APOE3/APOE3 and APOE4/APOE4 iPSC-derived mixed neurons at DIV49; donor had AD; baseline and 3-hour treatment with bafilomycin A1 and/or MG-132; mass-spectrometric protein abundance.

row.Finding description: In SH-SY5Y cells, 27-OHC produced stronger lysosomal δ-secretase activation with rApoE4 than with rApoE3. The authors also report leakage into the cytoplasm with rApoE4. Figure 1H–I represents three independent experiments.
row.Finding quote: Remarkably, 27-OHC strongly augmented δ-secretase levels and triggered its activation in the lysosomes in the presence of rApoE4, and the stimulatory effects were much stronger than with rApoE3. Notably, rApoE4 potently stimulated δ-secretase FL leakage from the lysosomes into the cytoplasm with most of active and truncated δ-secretase under rApoE4 and 27-OHC treatment.
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4, with 27-OHC) -> (stronger lysosomal δ-secretase activation and aberrant δ-secretase trafficking)
row.Experimental system: Human SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells treated with 100 nM rApoE3 or rApoE4 and 10 μM 27-OHC for three days. Lysosomal and cytosolic fractions were immunoblotted. The Results identify the secretion sample as rat neuronal medium, while the joint legend groups medium collection with SH-SY5Y fractionation.
row.Data location: Fig 1H-I, cited jointly; individual H/I allocation is not specified in supplied text.

proposed.why: Cleaved delta-secretase on immunoblots of lysosomal and cytosolic fractions is a surrogate for lysosomal enzyme activity and integrity, not a direct activity assay, and its rise can also come from higher expression.

row.Finding description: In the SH-SY5Y fractionation experiment, cholesterol failed to elicit cytosolic translocation of active δ-secretase. The authors also report no active-enzyme secretion under cholesterol, but the Results and legend give conflicting accounts of the medium source.
row.Finding quote: By contrast, cholesterol weakly activated δ-secretase in the lysosomes in the presence of rApoE4 but not rApoE3, but it failed to elicit active δ-secretase cytosolic translocation or secretion (Figure 1H-I).
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 and apoE4 cholesterol conditions) -> (no detected cytosolic translocation of active δ-secretase)
row.Experimental system: Human SH-SY5Y cells treated with 100 nM rApoE3 or rApoE4 and 50 μM cholesterol for three days, followed by subcellular fractionation and immunoblotting. The Results call the medium rat neuronal medium. The joint figure legend groups it with SH-SY5Y samples.
row.Data location: Fig 1H-I, cited jointly; individual H/I allocation is unspecified.

proposed.why: Fractionation immunoblot of active delta-secretase is a surrogate for lysosomal membrane integrity, not B itself; matched to the same assay in P9.F1 and P9.F3.

row.Finding description: In the SH-SY5Y experiment reported jointly in Fig 1H-I, cholesterol weakly activated lysosomal δ-secretase with apoE4 but not apoE3 across three independent experiments, indicating increased enzyme activation rather than demonstrated degradation failure.
row.Finding quote: By contrast, cholesterol weakly activated δ-secretase in the lysosomes in the presence of rApoE4 but not rApoE3, but it failed to elicit active δ-secretase cytosolic translocation or secretion (Figure 1H-I).
row.Finding summary: (apoE3 -> apoE4, with cholesterol) -> (weak lysosomal δ-secretase activation)
row.Experimental system: Human SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells; recombinant human apoE3 or apoE4, 100 nM, and cholesterol, 50 μM, for three days; lysosomal/cytosolic fractionation and immunoblotting.
row.Data location: Fig 1H-I, cited jointly; individual H/I allocation is unspecified.

proposed.why: Cleaved delta-secretase on lysosomal-fraction immunoblots is a surrogate for lysosomal enzyme activity, not a direct activity assay; matched to the same assay in P9.F1.

row.Finding description: Rapamycin induced autophagy-associated fluorescence in human ApoE3-expressing T98G cells but failed to induce it in ApoE4-expressing cells.
row.Finding quote: Rapamycin induced autophagy in T98G-E3 cells; however, it did not induce autophagy in T98G-E4 cells (Fig. 4g).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower rapamycin-induced autophagy-associated fluorescence)
row.Experimental system: Human glioblastoma T98G stable transformants expressing ApoE3 or ApoE4; 1 µM rapamycin; Abcam ab139484 autophagy-detection staining and fluorescence microscopy. The associated quantification reports three biological repeats, each with 15–20 images per group. This staining does not independently establish autophagic flux, and lipid metabolism was not measured.

row.Finding description: Quantified autophagy-associated fluorescence was lower in ApoE4-expressing than ApoE3-expressing human T98G cells under the reported autophagy-induction conditions.
row.Finding quote: Furthermore, measurement of autophagy in live cells showed that active autophagy levels were low in T98G-E4 cells compared to T98G-E3 cells.
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower autophagy-associated fluorescence)
row.Experimental system: Human glioblastoma T98G stable transformants expressing ApoE3 or ApoE4; fluorescence quantification per cell following Abcam ab139484 staining in the rapamycin/CBA2 experiment; three biological repeats with 15–20 images per group per experiment. Neither lipid metabolism nor lysosomal degradation flux was directly measured.

row.Finding description: After two weeks of thiorphan treatment, APOE4 mouse CA1 neurons showed larger and more abundant cathepsin D-positive lysosomes and more diffuse granular cathepsin D staining than APOE3 neurons, supporting altered lysosomal morphology without establishing impaired function.
row.Finding quote: Double-labeling confocal microscopy, using the lysosomal marker cathepsin D, revealed that the CA1 neurons of the thiorphan-treated apoE4 mice contained intracellular punctate cathepsin D-positive lysosomes, the size and levels of which were markedly higher than those of the corresponding apoE3 mice, as well as increased levels of diffused granular cathepsin D staining ( Fig. 8 ).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (larger and more abundant cathepsin D-positive lysosomes and increased diffuse cathepsin D staining)
row.Experimental system: Male human APOE3/3 versus APOE4/4 targeted-replacement mice, backcrossed eight generations to C57BL/6J, aged 3–4 months at experimentation; intracerebroventricular infusion of 0.5 mM thiorphan at 0.25 μl/h for two weeks; hippocampal CA1 neurons examined by cathepsin D/Aβ double-labeling confocal microscopy; no lipid manipulation, lysosomal enzyme activity assay, pH measurement, or degradation assay reported for this comparison.
row.Data location: Fig 8, cathepsin D images and associated lysosomal-activation Results paragraph

row.Finding description: Across three biological replicates, mouse astrocytes expressing human APOE4 had lysosomal pH elevated by >1 pH unit compared with APOE3 astrocytes, indicating impaired lysosomal acidification without testing lipid metabolism.
row.Finding quote: In contrast, we observed >1 pH unit elevation of lysosomal pH in ApoE4 astrocytes ( Fig. 3 C ).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher lysosomal pH in mouse astrocytes)
row.Experimental system: Cultured mouse astrocytes from ApoE-knockout mice with isogenic knock-in of human ApoE3 or ApoE4, supplied by David M. Holtzman; donor age and mouse background not specified. Lysosomal pH measured by ratiometric flow cytometry after 12 h loading with pHrodo-green–dextran and Alexa Fluor 647–dextran followed by a 6 h chase; ionophore-based calibration. These are mouse cells, not human brain cells; lipid metabolism was not measured.
